The hardware-in-the-loop experiment referred to an actual large-scale RPP project shows that the proposed strategy eliminates local over-voltage risks observed in existing strategies (up to 17.3%) and improves the faulted-phase voltage support capability by 17.48% on average across various fault conditions.

item.title: Preventive Control Optimization Against Voltage Oscillations Induced by Steady-State Repeated LVRT Based on Thevenin Equivalent Parameter Correction
item.description: Accelerated global energy transition towards low-carbon sources drives large-scale renewable integration, posing challenges to energy system security. In multi-renewable energy plants grid-connected systems (MREP-GCSs), repeated low voltage ride-through (LVRT) under steady-state can induce a novel switching oscillation. The oscillation stems from a self-sustaining cycle where, during steady-state operation, under certain grid conditions, increased active power output can trigger LVRT entry, which restores voltage and prompts LVRT exit, only for power restoration to immediately re-trigger the condition, causing persistent switching oscillations. Therefore, an optimized preventive control method is proposed against repeated LVRT, explicitly considering inter-plant influences in MREP-GCSs. Firstly, an assessment framework based on refined repeated LVRT occurrence conditions is developed. The re-derivation of this condition is based on equivalent parameters at the point of common coupling (PCC), considering the mutual power-voltage coupling between plants to correct the equivalent voltage. Secondly, a preventive control optimization method for repeated LVRT is developed from the perspective of online preventive control. To achieve precise regulation, a quantitative relationship between system-wide regulation variables combination and repeated LVRT boundary is established, along with other operating conditions, to form the constraints of the optimization model. The objective function aims to minimize regulation costs by coordinating grid-side and plant-side controls. This system-level method addresses the multi-plant boundary effects of control variables for coordinated multi-PCC control, optimizing grid-plant co-regulation to ensure renewable energy accommodation and enhance stability. Simulation results demonstrate the method accurately identifies repeated LVRT scenarios and suppresses oscillations.

item.title: Optimal Sizing of Energy Storage Systems for Grid-Forming Wind Turbines in Offshore Wind Farms
item.description: The high penetration of inverter-based resources, such as wind turbines (WTs), threatens power system stability due to their lack of inherent inertia. Therefore, equipping WTs with energy storage systems (ESSs) under grid-forming control, such as a virtual synchronous generator (VSG), is a promising solution. However, optimal ESS sizing remains challenging due to the wind stochasticity and the intricate coupling dynamics of VSGs. To address this challenge, this study proposes a stochastic dynamic optimization framework for ESS sizing in offshore wind farms (OWFs). Specifically, a unified frequency response model is developed using stochastic differential equations, explicitly incorporating Itô-process-based wind dynamics and the coupling between VSG voltage behavior and OWF power flow. On this basis, a stochastic dynamic optimization model is constructed to determine optimal ESS power and energy ratings. The key to converting this model into a tractable deterministic convex program lies in approximating stochastic expectations with Taylor-series-based assessment functions. To enable efficient large-scale optimization, the proposed framework employs a temporal decomposition strategy combined with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Simulations on a 36-turbine OWF validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, yielding an optimal ESS configuration with a power rating of 689–697 kW and an energy capacity of 19.88–19.95 kWh. Moreover, the solution strategy achieves a 77.9% reduction in solution time with only a 0.44% increase in the objective value.

item.title: Shaping the Q-U Droop Characteristic of Grid-Forming Converters From the Perspective of Constant Voltage Control
item.description: With the increasing penetration rate of variable renewable energy (VRE) and other inverter-based resources (IBR) in power systems, system inertia and strength are being continuously weakened. Grid-forming (GFM) technology, adaptable to weak grids, has attracted widespread attention. The GFM Q-U droop control is widely adopted in practice, but it is challenging to tune key parameters, such as initial voltage reference value and droop coefficient, therefore, the adaptability and effectiveness of voltage support is difficult to ensure. To take the advantages of GFM converters as voltage sources, adopting constant voltage control (CVC) seems to be a better choice. This paper clarifies the implicit internal connection between CVC and droop control, indicating that the droop characteristic does not inherently depend on droop control, but should be regarded as a natural external port performance under internal CVC. Based on above analysis, a novel shaping method for Q-U droop characteristic of GFM converters from the perspective of CVC using virtual impedance is proposed. The virtual impedance in the proposed method is straightforward to set due to its explicit physical meaning, and the method performs well in strong adaptability and robustness for both islanded and grid-connected modes. Finally, the conclusions and the control effectiveness are verified by theoretical analysis, simulation, and experimental results.

item.title: Power Coupling Mechanism Analysis and Hierarchical Adaptive Decoupling Control for Wind Farm Connected to Weak Grid
item.description: Active frequency and voltage support from wind turbine generators (WTGs) improves grid stability. However, when connected to weak grid, phase-locked loop (PLL) tracking inaccuracies can cause inadequate power decoupling in WTGs. This issue is further aggravated by uneven wind speeds and spatial structure within wind farm (WF), ultimately undermining overall support capability. To address this problem, this paper firstly systematically investigates the influence of multiple factors on the coupling power from the unit, farm, to grid levels. Specifically, PLL bandwidth and grid strength affect the tracking performance of the PLL, while wind speed distribution and spatial structure influence the operating points of WTGs and the coupling transmission between nodes, respectively. On the basis, the Hierarchical Adaptive Decoupling Control (HADC) strategy for WF is proposed, which mitigate the coupling power by introducing quantified power coupling components into the power outer-loop control of rotor-side converter. To improve the applicability and robustness, the main parameters of HADC adaptively vary according to load changes and wind speed distribution. It enables to reduce the power coupling degree and improve frequency and voltage support capability of WF. Finally, case studies are conducted on a real WF project in Bazhou, Xinjiang, China. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

item.title: A Unified Framework for Multi-Stability Constrained Optimization in IBR-Dominated Power Systems
item.description: Conventional optimization frameworks for power-system operation and planning primarily focus on steady-state conditions, which become increasingly inadequate as rising penetrations of inverter-based resources (IBRs) strengthen the coupling between stability and steady-state operating conditions. Meanwhile, the software-defined nature of IBRs provides additional flexibility to co-optimize operating points and dynamic behavior. This paper proposes a unified stability-constrained optimization framework that incorporates synchronization, voltage, and frequency stability within a single scheduling model. Established stability criteria are selected and translated into explicit operational limits, after which a general formulation is developed to embed all three criteria in a common structure. The resulting second-order cone (SOC) constraints are convex and can be integrated seamlessly into existing optimization models. The proposed framework enables the simultaneous pursuit of economic efficiency and multi-dimensional stability enhancement, providing a tractable pathway for secure operation in future IBR-dominated power systems.

item.title: Flexibilizing Grid-Connected Renewable Power to Ammonia Systems via a Novel Hydrogen Storage Design: Configuration and Operational Strategy
item.description: Renewable power to ammonia (ReP2A) offers a promising route for renewable energy utilization. To fully utilize volatile renewable generation without breaking process continuity, ReP2A systems require hydrogen storage subsystems with storage tanks and compressors. However, the conventional layout of hydrogen storage subsystems can cause significant hydrogen supply pressure variations, restricting the ReP2A system to a semi-steady-state operation inadequate for handling renewable fluctuations. In practice, feedforward control based on short-term forecasts is widely employed, yet forecast errors necessitate substantial grid electricity purchases to maintain continuity. This coupling between power and chemical manufacturing increases grid peak-shaving pressure and undermines economic benefits. To address these challenges, a novel hydrogen storage subsystem with a parallel-connected compressor is proposed to enhance pressure regulation, alongside a capacity allocation method and a state-transition-based PID (ST-PID) control strategy. Furthermore, a multi-timescale framework embeds the ST-PID controller to bridge real-time control and long-term optimization. Case studies with real-world data demonstrate that the proposed system unlocks the flexibility for renewable consumption and shows robustness against prediction errors, reducing grid electricity reliance by 38.56% and lowering the levelized cost of ammonia by 8.75%. This offers dual benefits in promoting renewable integration and enhancing economic performance.

item.title: Dual-Port DC Wind Turbines Based Offshore Wind Power Integration System Embedded With Power Balance and Fault Ride-Through Capability
item.description: In offshore wind farm (OWF) integration systems, emerging DC collection and transmission schemes (all-DC) necessitate the series-parallel connection of DC wind turbines (WTs) to boost the DC collection voltage. However, power imbalance among DC WTs impairs the overall efficiency of the integration system. To address the inherent limitations of the all-DC approach, this paper proposes a dual-port DC wind turbine-based DC collection and transmission topology for OWF integration. Where the DC ports of each DC WT are connected in series to elevate the DC collection voltage, while the AC ports of adjacent DC WTs are connected to decouple the power of DC WTs. Firstly, the topology, operating principle and control strategy of the all-DC integration system incorporating the proposed DC WT are introduced, and the power balance mechanism is analyzed. Then, a comprehensive fault ride-through (FRT) method is proposed to handle various fault types. Furthermore, the parameter design method and overall evaluation of the proposed integration system are conducted. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed all-DC integration system under different operation scenarios is validated in PSCAD/EMTDC.

item.title: Lightweight Series-Connected Topology and Control Strategy for Megawatt-Scale High-Altitude Wind Energy Systems
item.description: Scaling high-altitude wind energy systems (HAWESs) to the megawatt level faces a “weight–voltage” paradox: reducing tether mass requires medium voltage, yet conventional voltage-boosting components add prohibitive airborne mass. This paper resolves the paradox with a novel architecture using series-connected, diode-rectified generators, which inherently builds medium transmission voltage without onboard converters or transformers, enabling an ultralight airborne system controlled solely by a grid-side converter (GSC) located on the ground. A small-signal stability analysis considering generator parameter heterogeneity reveals that the system is robust to moderate wind variations, but becomes unstable when wind-speed heterogeneity drives a turbine into a region of positive torque–speed slope. The precise identification of this physical stability boundary provides the crucial design guidance needed to unlock a practical pathway toward the deployment of utility-scale HAWESs.

item.title: Multi-Mode Response Mechanism and Fault Ride-Through Control for Renewable Energy Integrated System via Grid-Forming VSC-HVDC
item.description: The renewable energy integrated system via grid-forming voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) has become a critical pathway for modern power systems. Existing studies have not adequately considered the impact of abrupt variations in the equivalent grid impedance under symmetrical faults on the power angle response, or the control interaction between the virtual synchronous generator-based grid-end converter (VSG-GEC) and the renewable energy-end converter (REEC), which may lead to power angle instability of VSG-GEC or cause severe disturbances to the renewable energy island. This paper analyzes the power-angle characteristics of VSG-GEC and reveals a multi-mode response mechanism resulting from the interaction between the outer-loop controller of VSG-GEC and the faulted grid with equivalent impedance variation. The constraints on the control reference values of VSG-GEC are derived to prevent power angle instability and avoid AC overcurrent, thereby establishing a fault ride-through feasible region considering multi-mode responses. A fault ride-through control method based on response mode adjustment is then developed. Validation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains uninterrupted operation of the grid-forming integrated system while maximizing the active power of VSG-GEC to reduce the REEC control adjustment required to avoid DC overvoltage, thereby mitigating disturbances to the renewable energy island.

item.title: Bilevel Optimization for Green Hydrogen-to-Ammonia Synthesis System Considering Complex Dynamic Processes and Uncertainties
item.description: The wind-powered green hydrogen-to-ammonia system offers a promising pathway for utilizing marine renewable energy; however, its economic viability is constrained by the strongly nonlinear dynamics of ammonia synthesis and the inherent stochasticity of wind power generation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a bilevel scheduling framework. In the upper layer, a reduced-order Trend- and Structure-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (TS-PINN) model is developed by embedding trend priors and mechanistic constraints, effectively capturing the nonlinear characteristics of the ammonia synthesis process with significantly reduced computational effort. An improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm is then employed to co-optimize operational strategies and key reactor setpoints, including bed temperature and pressure. In the lower layer, a Wasserstein-distance-based distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model is established to coordinate hydrogen production and storage operations to hedge against wind power uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an effective balance among modeling accuracy, economic performance, and operational robustness, while accounting for coupled reaction–heat-transfer dynamics and renewable generation uncertainty.

item.title: Event-Driven Restoration of Interconnected Distribution Systems With R-SOPs Adapting to Continuous Disasters and Uncertainties
item.description: Extreme disasters lead to continuous and large-scale faults in distribution systems (DSs), posing challenges in developing practical restoration strategies. This paper proposes a pre-disaster prevention and post-disaster restoration framework for R-SOP-enabled interconnected distribution systems (IDSs), which accounts for the persistence of faults during evolution and the uncertainties in renewable energy source and load. Unlike most existing studies that focus on individual DSs and fixed fault scenarios, this paper employs a reconfigurable soft open point (R-SOP) with asymmetric converter design. Through its feeder selection and converter reconfiguration mechanisms, the R-SOP enables efficient capacity utilization and dynamic interconnection among multiple DSs, and additionally addresses, in a unified manner, the dual uncertainties of stochastic fluctuations and sudden faults under continuous disasters. In the pre-disaster phase, electric buses (EBs) are deployed based on proactive restoration simulations to reduce potential load shedding and shorten post-disaster travel distances. In the post-disaster phase, an event-driven restoration method is developed, wherein predefined fault events and error events dynamically update restoration strategies to adapt to continuous faults and uncertainties. By combining R-SOP-assisted reconfiguration with coordinated scheduling of flexible resources, the proposed method overcomes the limitations of individual-network restoration, enhancing system resilience. Simulation results based on a modified 102-node IDS show that the proposed method not only accelerates service restoration under continuous extreme disaster events but also ensures voltage security.

item.title: Dynamic Interaction Modeling and Stability Analysis for Grid-Connected Renewable Energy Systems With High Inertia Energy Storage Synchronous Condenser
item.description: The high inertia energy storage synchronous condenser (HIESSC), which integrates the doubly-fed machine technology with flywheel energy storage, has recently emerged as a promising means to support both frequency and voltage regulation in renewable energy sources (RESs). Despite its novelty, the impact of the HIESSC on system oscillations and the interactions among the control loops of RES stations remains unclear. This paper examines a grid-connected system comprising the HIESSC and a grid-connected converter with grid-following control (GCC-GFL). Firstly, a single-input-single-output interaction model is developed through equivalent block diagram transformations. By incorporating the grid-side coupling impedance and transfer functions of interacting subsystems, the proposed model reveals how the HIESSC modifies the dynamic characteristics of GCC-GFL through a feedback control perspective. Subsequently, the impact of HIESSC operating modes and operating points on the small-signal stability is analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed methods and analyses is validated by the experiments.

item.title: Hybrid Fault Isolation and Power Control of Wind Turbine Generators Based on Stacked UIO
item.description: The stable operation of megawatt-class wind turbines directly impacts grid connection performance. As complex electromechanicald systems operating in variable environments, time-varying hybrid faults frequently occur, posing challenges for fault-tolerant control (FTC). This paper proposes novel approaches for hybrid fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant controller design. First, a collaborative architecture for a stacked unknown input observer (UIO) is constructed for integrated fault diagnosis of hybrid faults in wind turbine generators (WTGs). The designed stacked UIO strategy can decouple and separately estimate the dynamic of speed and torque, achieving effective time-varying hybrid fault diagnosis. Second, given the disturbances, uncertainties, and discrete-time nature of WTGs, the asymptotic stability of the proposed UIO is established using Lyapunov’s theorem. Finally, combining fault information, a two-degree-of-freedom model predictive control strategy is adopted to achieve FTC while also considering power stability tracking. Simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate time-varying faults in WTG actuators and sensors, and maintain reliable control performance under hybrid fault conditions, thereby verifying its effectiveness as a comprehensive FTC solution.

item.title: Graph Neural Network With Dual-Stream Attention for Global Maximum Power Point Tracking Under Partial Shading Conditions
item.description: Due to the complex nonlinear coupling between circuit topology and environmental changes, precise maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions remains a challenge. Existing data-driven methods typically view photovoltaic (PV) arrays as unstructured feature vectors or Euclidean grids, which fail to capture the fundamental series-parallel constraints that control the distribution of current and voltage. This study proposes a graph neural network with dual-stream attention (GNN-DSA), which is a physical perception framework that can strictly decouple static topologies from dynamic environmental signals. Static streams encode arrays into message-passed directed graphs with specific edge types that capture series-parallel circuit constraints, while dynamic streams capture irradiation patterns through the Transformer. A novel bidirectional cross-attention mechanism explicitly simulates the interaction between circuit constraints and environmental stress. Hardware verification indicates that the tracking efficiency of GNN-DSA on real PV panels is 99.1%–99.6%, on solar array simulators is 99.99%, and the response time is less than 100 ms. Comparative analysis shows that compared with the multilayer perceptron baseline, GNN-DSA reduces the mean squared error by 45.6%, and compared with the state-of-the-art Crossformer model, it reduces it by 22.3%.

item.title: Multi-Source Coordinated Frequency Control of Grid-Connected Wind-Solar-Storage Power Station With Economic Improvement
item.description: Renewable power plant participating in frequency regulation often compromises power generation efficiency, and existing frequency regulation strategies generally neglect economic cost. To improve frequency security and economic efficiency, the paper proposes a multi-source coordinated frequency control (MCFC) for wind-solar-storage hybrid power stations. The MCFC control consists of two stages: frequency support and frequency recovery. During frequency support, photovoltaic (PV), wind, and energy storage are sequentially activated according to dynamic characteristics. The strategy allocates wind, PV, and energy storage outputs based on frequency security constraints to avoid excessive use of regulation energy and improve economic efficiency. During frequency recovery, wind turbine rotor speed is smoothly restored, and the recovery of the energy storage system (ESS) state of charge (SOC) is explicitly considered. Case studies are undertaken on the two-area power system with a wind-solar-storage hybrid power station and Guangshui hybrid collection station. The results show that MCFC can restore the frequency above safety thresholds and minimize renewable regulation energy to improve economic efficiency. Compared with existing methods, MCFC not only restores frequency to 49.5 Hz under a wider range of disturbances but also reduces economic index by up to 40% under mild disturbances.

item.title: An Adaptive Graph Convolution-Based Bi-Level Planning Strategy for Urban Fast-Charging Stations in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks
item.description: To address the mismatch between massive charging requirement triggers and limited charging resource supply in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks (ETCNs), this paper proposes a bi-level planning strategy for urban fast-charging stations (FCSs). First, given the topological interdependence and feature interactions of ETCNs, a unified graph-structured representation model is constructed to characterize the dynamic transmission of energy and information among multiple agents in “vehicles-stations-networks”. Second, adaptive graph convolution is designed in the upper layer. Through multi-order neighborhood aggregation and adaptive weights, the inherent physical-electrical correlation knowledge among multiple agents is learned, enabling multi-dimensional feature extraction of ETCNs and differentiated weight allocation to transportation nodes. The physical constraints of ETCN operation are embedded in the feature loss as regularization, thereby constructing a semi-supervised learning paradigm driven by data-feature collaboration loss. Then, based on the candidate FCS set initially screened by the upper layer, an equilibrium evaluation index is established to suppress node congestion and service blind areas. In the lower layer, a multi-objective optimization model is constructed to jointly solve the connection location of FCSs in the electricity network and the capacity configuration of charging piles. Finally, case studies are conducted within a practical functional zone in Hong Kong, China. Experimental results verify the superiority of the proposed method under different planning scenarios.

item.title: Anticipatory Utility Operations With Long-Duration Hydrogen Storage and Carbon Market Synergies
item.description: When leveraged within carbon market mechanisms, hydrogen energy storage systems (HESS) offer a viable option for supporting low-carbon operation in vertically integrated utilities. However, a key challenge is that short-term operational decisions are made without explicit visibility of their long-term consequences, which are reflected through cumulative hydrogen and carbon constraints that ensure system feasibility. To bridge this time-scale gap, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning–augmented primal–dual rolling-horizon optimization framework. A trained future-aware regularizer incorporates long-term information into short-term decision-making, while a primal–dual scheme enforces cumulative constraints on hydrogen and carbon markets with computational tractability. Numerical studies on the IEEE 6-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus test systems demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework keeps annual terminal residuals negligible while reducing peak emissions, improving economic performance, and enabling seasonal load shifting across different system scales.

item.title: Rotor-Angle Stability Enhancement Control for MMC-MTDC Systems Without Sending-End Power Reserves
item.description: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems are increasingly integrated into AC grids, making rotor-angle stability more critical. Improper HVDC dynamics during disturbances may weaken synchronizing torque and damping, thereby aggravating oscillations. This paper investigates the offshore wind farm (OWF)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) system and analyzes the impact of its power injections on grid rotor-angle stability. On this basis, a frequency-based power control logic is first proposed to enhance rotor-angle stability. Building on this logic, Lyapunov-based control laws are derived to coordinate active and reactive power both among multiple terminals (inter-terminal level) and within each converter under capacity constraints (intra-terminal level). To further optimize the coordinated control, an optimization framework is then designed, ensuring effective and secure support. Finally, considering the absence of power reserves at the sending-end OWF, a capacitor energy-based control strategy is proposed for MTDC systems to utilize all MMCs’ capacitor energy at the same time for stability support (device level), thereby expanding the available support energy and further improving rotor-angle stability. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control are validated on the IEEE 39-bus system via PSCAD/EMTDC and MATLAB co-simulation.

item.title: Risk Assessment of Forced SSO Excited by DFIG-Originated Interharmonics
item.description: The forced subsynchronous oscillations (FSSOs) induced by the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-originated interharmonics can degrade power quality and threaten the security of equipment as well as the power system. This study investigates the generation mechanisms of DFIG-originated interharmonics, and proposes a novel criterion of the impedance-based method that reveals the excitation mechanisms of FSSOs. Subsequently, a severity index for FSSOs, defined as the interharmonic amplitude ratio (IAR), is established to quantify the FSSO severity. A methodology is developed to compute the probability distribution of this severity function, incorporating the probabilistic characteristics of system operating conditions and wind speeds. Building upon this severity index and its probability distribution, a risk matrix integrating two distinct risk dimensions, power quality degradation risk and equipment/system security risks, is constructed to assess FSSO risk. The proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive time-domain simulations. Simulation results demonstrate that both risk types are highly sensitive to the probabilistic characteristics of grid operating conditions and wind speed profiles. Specifically, when the grid operates with high probability under weak-grid conditions, and the DFIG rotor frequency corresponding to average wind speed falls within 5/6∼7/6 times the fundamental frequency, the system experiences elevated levels of both FSSO-induced risks.

item.title: Scheduling for Hybrid Microgrids With Renewable Energy Sources and Hydrogen Storage: Data-Correlated Uncertainty Modeling and Semi-Convex Relaxation
item.description: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), hydrogen energy storage (HES), and electric vehicles (EVs) is critical to the decarbonization of electric power production; however, it introduces significant challenges for microgrid energy management owing principally to RES uncertainty and the non-convex constraints associated with HES and EV operations. The present work addresses these challenges by applying data-driven uncertainty set optimization and semi-convex relaxation approaches. First, a probability-driven data-correlated uncertainty set is developed using historical data distributions to generate RES uncertainty representations with reduced conservativeness under significantly reduced computational burden. Second, a closed-loop semi-convex relaxation procedure is designed to manage the non-convex operational constraints of HES and EV operations, where the NP-hard nature of these constraints is addressed by iteratively enforcing only violated binary conditions, which ensures solution accuracy with minimal computational overhead. Third, the resulting tri-level robust energy management model is solved efficiently by a customized column-and-constraint generation algorithm incorporating the proposed relaxation procedure. As a result, only those non-convex constraints that are violated in the relaxed solution are included in the energy management solution process. The superiority of the proposed approach over existing state-of-the-art methods in enabling higher penetrations of clean energy technologies is demonstrated through numerical case studies on a practical hybrid microgrid system.

item.title: Distributed Adaptive Coordination of Flexibility Resources for Real-Time Power Balancing in Islanded DC Microgrids
item.description: Modern DC microgrids (DC-MGs) typically incorporate Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), energy storage systems, and local loads. In islanded DC-MGs, effective coordination of these components is essential for secure and reliable operation, given the intermittent nature of RESs and the uncertain demand profile. This paper employs electric spring topology to enhance flexibility through the smart management of both energy stored in batteries, and loads, in the case that the generation capacity of multiple RESs—operating with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm—is insufficient to meet demand. Besides, a distributed adaptive droop-based scheme is designed concerning a trade-off between common bus voltage regulation and proper current/power sharing among units. This distributed scheme benefits from a low-bandwidth communication interface among the in-service units to collect required data for adaptive estimation of droop gains. To ensure reliable operation of the DC-MG, batteries' capacity and State-of-Charge (SoC) information are also incorporated into the energy-sharing strategy, aiming to maintain SoC balance among storage units during replenishment. The feasibility of the proposed approach is evaluated through a Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) platform.

item.title: Available-Power-Constrained Coordinated Fault Voltage Support Control for Multiple Inverter-Interfaced DGs
item.description: The increasing prevalence of weak grid conditions necessitates that inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDGs) support voltage during faults to prevent further disturbances. However, maximizing IIDGs’ voltage support capability while respecting operational constraints to prevent unintended tripping remains challenging. This paper proposes an available-power-constrained coordinated fault voltage support control strategy for multiple IIDGs. First, based on the fault characteristics of resistive-inductive distribution networks (DN), a current reference strategy is developed to maximize each IIDG’s voltage support contribution. Then, considering constraints of non-fault-phase voltage and power fluctuation, the safe operating domain of each IIDG is derived. On this basis, an adaptive fault voltage support control framework is constructed, where a zonal clustering method enables communication free coordinated control among multiple IIDGs. In addition, the applicable condition of the proposed method is quantified using the grid short-circuit ratio (SCR) of the grid. Simulation results show that, for case of SCR lower than 3, the proposed method can improve the fault voltage of DNs by 30.8%.

item.title: Stability Analysis and Parametric Feasible-Region Characterization of Multi-Oscillation Modes in GFL-GFM Hybrid Systems Under Wide Scale Grid Strength
item.description: This paper investigates the stability of multi-low-frequency oscillation (LFO) modes in grid-connected hybrid systems with grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) converters. The objective is to reveal the coupling oscillation mechanism between dual-source power and control parameters under wide variations in grid strength, and to construct a stable operating domain. A reduced-order model balancing accuracy and complexity is established, and a decoupled equivalent damping analysis method is proposed to quantitatively characterize the stability of the dominant GFL and GFM oscillation modes from the perspective of damping formation mechanism. It is found that the GFL-dominated and GFM-dominated oscillation modes exhibit opposite stability evolution trends with respect to grid strength and are constrained by the dual-source power coupling effect. As a result, a single fixed parameter set cannot ensure stable system operation across a wide range of grid strengths and full power operating conditions. Furthermore, the influence of key control parameters on the oscillation modes is clarified, and stable parameter boundaries under extreme operating conditions are determined. Time-domain simulations validate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the proposed stable domain construction method.

item.title: Enhanced Frequency Regulation Utilizing Wind Power: Model Predictive Control Considering Adjustable Capacity of Wind Turbines
item.description: Random wind speed fluctuations can significantly influence a wind turbine's ability to release rotor kinetic energy during frequency regulation. To fully exploit the turbine's adjustable capacity, this paper establishes a dynamic model of a doubly fed induction generator and derives its adjustable capacity considering ultra-short-term wind speed forecasting. The nonlinear states are then projected into a high-dimensional linear space with the Koopman operator, enabling accurate global linearization. Based on this model, a distributed, capacity-aware Model Predictive Control (cVMPC) framework is formulated, where the ‘c’ denotes its core feature: capacity-awareness. To further improve performance, the adjustable capacity parameter is proactively predicted and incorporated into the MPC's control weighting coefficients. This enables an adaptive regulation strategy that explicitly accounts for the predicted kinetic energy reserves of each turbine. The proposed cVMPC approach is validated on a 3-machine, 9-bus system. Simulation results confirm that the strategy alleviates the initial frequency nadir, accelerates rotor speed recovery, and prevents secondary frequency dips.

item.title: Exploring the Flexibility of Twin-Basin Tidal Range Power Plants Through Optimal Control
item.description: In twin-basin tidal range schemes, a type of tidal barrage with two water reservoirs, the variations in sea water level throughout the day are used to generate electrical power, without direct CO2 emissions. This study focuses on optimising the operation of twin-basin tidal barrages using different objective functions, namely: energy maximising, income maximising and demand matching. The novelty of the study relies on using moment-based control to transcribe the infinite-dimensional twin-basin barrage optimal control problem into a finite-dimensional nonlinear program. To test the controller performance, a case study in the Severn Estuary, in the Southwest of the U.K., is presented, where the tidal resource is one of the highest in the world. It is found that, under tailored optimal scheduling, the twin-basin scheme can effectively shift generation periods to achieve greater income (between 1% and 3%, in the income maximising case) or to match peak demand hours (in the demand matching case), showing the increased flexibility of tidal range power plants compared to more traditional renewables. In the study cases presented, there is general agreement between energy maximising and demand matching optimal operation, since, for the particular time interval chosen, the phase of the tide was well aligned with demand, suggesting that tidal range plants are inherently demand-following. Furthermore, a control strategy is proposed for twin-basin barrages that results in continuous power output, reducing the hours of stand-by of the turbines, and highlighting the potential of twin-basin barrage for clean and dispatchable electricity generation.

item.title: Mitigating Power Fluctuations of Large Language Model Training via Hybrid Energy Storage Systems in Renewable-Powered Computing Centers
item.description: As the demand for computing power surges, renewable-powered computing centers (RPCCs) are being deployed at an accelerating pace. During large language model (LLM) training, RPCCs exhibit highly fluctuating, broadband load characteristics that can excite grid resonances and thereby pose significant threats to the secure and stable operation of emerging power systems. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) planning approach tailored to mitigate the power fluctuations of RPCCs. First, a signal decomposition method based on symplectic geometric mode decomposition (SGMD) is developed to capture multi-timescale load power fluctuations, on top of which a HESS power allocation strategy is designed. Then, by explicitly accounting for the power fluctuation characteristics of LLM training, an energy storage demand assessment method is established and a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model for HESS planning is formulated. Finally, case studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed planning framework and to elucidate the impacts of power fluctuations inherent to different LLM training tasks.

item.title: ShadowSense: Edge Optimized Self-Supervised Learning for Dynamic Shadow Mapping of Solar Panels
item.description: We introduce ShadowSense, a self-supervised, edge-deployable framework for dynamic shadow mapping and short-term PV power forecasting. Unlike prior methods that require labor-intensive manual annotations or rely on overly complex physical models, ShadowSense uses transient power dips as weak supervision signals, enabling fully unsupervised learning from synchronized sky imagery and power measurements. The architecture integrates a masked spatiotemporal autoencoder to learn cloud motion dynamics, a differentiable geometric projection module to adapt to diverse panel orientations, and a causal alignment system to maintain temporal correspondence between cloud shadows and power responses. Evaluated over 122,400 observations across 92 days in Kaunas, Lithuania, the system achieved a 32.7% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) compared to baselines, captured 92.3% of rapid power ramps, and operated with an average inference latency of 66 ms and energy cost of 0.52 J per prediction on a solar-powered NVIDIA Jetson Nano, demonstrating scalable, real-time PV forecasting in resource-constrained environments.

item.title: Optimal Operation Strategy for AA-CAES in Joint Energy and Regulation Markets: Managing SoC Deviations From Regulation Response
item.description: As a representative technology of physical long-duration energy storage, advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) is capable of providing joint energy and secondary frequency regulation (SFR) services, playing an important role in power system regulation. However, the nonlinear characteristics of AA-CAES poses a challenge, as tracking regulation signals induces shifts in the operating point and air consumption of AA-CAES, complicating the process for state-of-charge (SoC) management. This paper proposes an optimal operation strategy for AA-CAES in joint energy and SFR markets. First, the SoC deviation induced by regulation response of AA-CAES is analyzed, and a dynamic operation model for AA-CAES to provide joint energy and SFR capacity services incorporating deviation impacts is developed. Subsequently, a self-scheduling strategy accounting for the uncertainty of regulation signals is proposed. This strategy employs stochastic dynamic programming to construct value functions in the day-ahead stage, and develops a chance-constrained stochastic programming model for rolling optimization in the intra-day stage. Numerical simulations based on real-world AA-CAES plant data validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The results indicate that considering the SoC deviations increases the net revenue by 3.0%, while the adoption of chance constraints leads to net revenue increase of 4.3%.

item.title: Supervisory Control Framework for a Hybrid PV-BESS Inverter Under Power Export Constraint
item.description: This paper presents a practical supervisory energy management framework for a hybrid photovoltaic (PV)-battery energy storage system (BESS) inverter operating under a grid export constraint. The strategy reconciles two conflicting objectives: to maximize PV energy utilization and to minimize BESS cycling energy while requiring almost no inverter firmware modification. Unlike conventional inverter-embedded methods with limited control flexibility, the proposed framework introduces a vendor-independent supervisory controller that interfaces with a hybrid inverter through standard Modbus/RS-485 communication. A compact five-mode control architecture enables rapid adaptation to load variations, improved PV operating point selection, and coordinated BESS dispatch with minimal cycling stress. Experimental validation across eight representative scenarios spanning seasonal irradiance variability and weekday/weekend load patterns demonstrates significant performance gains. During summer, spring, and autumn, grid import decreases by 93%, the self-sufficiency ratio increases from 45.7–65.5% to 74.6–78.9%, and PV curtailment decreases consistently. Furthermore, the annual grid expenditure is reduced by nearly 80%. Economic analysis indicates favorable viability, with a payback period of 1.9 years when accounting for grid savings and conservative BESS lifetime extension benefits. The proposed supervisory energy management system achieves superior PV utilization, enhanced operational autonomy, and substantial economic benefits, offering a scalable, retrofit-compatible solution for export-constrained residential and commercial PV-BESS installations.

item.title: HyMoOpt: A Hybrid Momentum Optimizer for Axial Induction Factor Control of Wind Farm Under Dynamic Wake Effects
item.description: This paper addresses the real-time axial induction factor (AIF) control problem for large-scale wind farms under dynamic wake effects and uncertain wind conditions. We first establish the mathematical formulation for the AIF control problem. The objective is to optimize collective power output while balancing the trade-off between energy revenue and the degradation of turbine lifespan caused by AIF adjustments. Building upon this foundation, we propose a novel hybrid momentum optimizer (HyMoOpt) controller. It combines a model-based gradient estimator for rapid convergence with a model-free feedback mechanism for robustness against model mismatch. A momentum term is further integrated to accelerate convergence and damp oscillations. We then derive an analytical bound on the gradient approximation error and prove that the proposed control algorithm achieves a sublinear convergence rate to the stationary point. Finally, the practical efficacy of HyMoOpt is demonstrated through simulations on a realistic 93-turbine offshore wind farm. Results show that it significantly enhances power output while maintaining strong adaptability under dynamic operational scenarios.

item.title: Robust Coordinated Prescriptive Power System Dispatch: Bridging Adjustable Robust OPF and Multiple Probabilistic Predictions
item.description: The increasing penetration of renewable generation introduces substantial uncertainty into short-term power system operations, challenging cost-effective dispatch under network constraints. In conventional predict–then–optimize frameworks, uncertainty bounds are learned independently and treated as fixed inputs to robust optimal power flow (OPF), limiting feedback from operational decisions to improve uncertainty representation. This paper proposes a robust semi-end-to-end coordinated decision framework that bridges probabilistic forecasting and robust optimization for prescriptive power system dispatch. Probabilistic prediction models estimate one-step-ahead renewable generation and load intervals, which are incorporated into a robust OPF model through the induced uncertainty sets. The proposed framework integrates three components: a machine learning layer, a robust decision-making layer, and a decision evaluation layer. During the forward pass, predicted uncertainty bounds are converted into robust dispatch decisions, while in the backward pass, gradients are propagated through the optimization layer to train forecasting models using task-level operational feedback. Numerical results demonstrate stable training and consistent economic improvements over the conventional predict–then–optimize approach, achieving average total-cost reductions of 14.3% and 16.0% on the IEEE 5- and 30-bus systems, respectively. The improvement on the IEEE 118-bus system is smaller because uncertainty-related costs account for a limited portion of total operating costs. Under the adopted single-interval DC-based dispatch formulation, the proposed method also learns tighter uncertainty intervals (around 25% narrower) while reducing reserve-related slack activation under stressed operating conditions.

item.title: Optimal Frequency Trajectory-Guided Emergency Frequency Control for Receiving-End Grids
item.description: Aiming to enhance frequency support strength of receiving-end power grids, this paper presents an optimal frequency trajectory (OFT)-guided emergency frequency control strategy. The proposed methodology comprises three core components: First, an OFT-based system frequency response model is developed, incorporating wind farm frequency regulation characteristics while ensuring rotor speed self-recovery during primary frequency regulation. Second, a frequency support strength requirement evaluation model is established to determine necessary system inertia and frequency regulation capacity under frequency security limits. Third, a coordinated emergency frequency control strategy is proposed, enabling optimal power adjustment across multiple frequency regulation resources through virtual inertia and virtual droop parameter conversion. A dedicated compensation mechanism is integrated to address primary frequency regulation deadband effects. The effectiveness of the proposed models and control strategy is verified through comparative case studies using modified IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus test systems. Under the HVDC blocking scenario, the proposed approach reduces the maximum frequency deviation by 51.25% and achieves a cost-saving improvement of over 50% relative to the benchmarked existing methods.

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Coordination of Heterogeneous Electrolyzers: A Federated Reinforcement Learning Approach With Safety Guarantees
item.description: The complementarity between high-flexibility Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) and low-cost Alkaline (ALK) electrolyzers contributes to the synergistic development of green power and hydrogen sectors. However, wide-range renewable power fluctuations impose technical challenges on the optimal power allocation among these heterogeneous PEM and ALK units, which might result in safety violations and operational inefficiency. To address these challenges, this study proposes a privacy-preserving, physics-informed federated multi-agent control framework. Specifically, the architecture leverages a federated learning paradigm to aggregate decentralized strategies with limited direct data exchange, while incorporating an LSTM-enhanced algorithm to resolve partial observability by tracking long-timescale multiphysics dynamics like thermodynamic evolution and gas purity. Furthermore, a dual-tier proactive defense mechanism integrating a robust risk predictor with a quadratic programming projection layer is designed to strictly enforce hard physical constraints. Numerical results verify that the proposed approach effectively balances data privacy, physical safety, and precise regulation performance.

item.title: Short-Term Frequency Regulation for Wind Farms via Stochastic Distribution Control and Image-Based Visual Servoing
item.description: Large-scale wind farms (WFs) are increasingly required to participate in short-term frequency regulation (STFR) during frequency events. To enhance the stability, accuracy, responsiveness, and rapidity of the STFR capability while mitigating the fatigue load of wind turbines, a novel model-free STFR strategy is proposed in this paper based on stochastic distribution control (SDC) theory and image-based visual servoing (IBVS) method for WFs with numerous WTs. The histogram of the frequency is used to guide the WF to implement STFR. By comparing current histogram features with target features, the target frequency histogram tracking control is realized. Meanwhile, by minimizing the active power reference fluctuations for each WT, the fatigue load of each WT is reduced. The optimal active power reference is allocated to individual WTs directly without adopting aggregation and dis-aggregation methods. The simulation results show that the proposed control method improves the STFR capability in terms of stability, accuracy, responsiveness, and rapidity.

item.title: Optimal Volt-VAR Curve Design for Inverter-Based Resources in Distribution Grids
item.description: The electric distribution grid has undergone rapid evolution, with customers increasingly adopting distributed energy resources (DERs). Conventional grid devices, like static reactive power compensators, were installed to address specific operational needs under traditional load conditions and are often not automated, making them less effective in today’s dynamic grid. Uncoordinated DER operation can further exacerbate issues, causing overvoltage, reverse reactive power flow, substation congestion, and low load power factor (LPF), highlighting the limitations of legacy grid assets. This paper presents an innovative methodology to design optimal volt-VAR curves (VVCs) for inverters to mitigate these challenges. To facilitate convergence and accelerate the computation of the optimal power flow (OPF) problem, a linear three-phase network power flow solver is employed to minimize reactive power flow through the substation and enhance the voltage profile within the distribution grid. Unlike existing approaches that use static VVCs or determine VVCs for each time instant, the proposed method generates an optimal VVC for each PV inverter over a specified period, while also producing location-specific curves. The approach is demonstrated on the IEEE 123-Node feeder and a large-scale real feeder with multiple PV inverters, showing improvements in substation LPF and feeder voltage profiles.

item.title: Multi-Mode Synchronization Control for Standalone Multi-Solar-Wind-Battery Storage System With Autonomous Transition and Improved Power Quality
item.description: This paper presents a modular distribution-level standalone microgrid topology and control strategy for remote-area applications, integrating multiple solar photovoltaic (SPV) arrays and variable-speed doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)–based wind energy systems. Proposed architecture supports coordinated operation of AC loads, low- and medium-voltage DC loads, and electric vehicle (EV) charging through a common DC bus, enhancing flexibility and scalability. In standalone operation, nonlinear and fluctuating loads, frequent mode transitions, and synchronization requirements to AC bus introduce significant stator harmonics and transient disturbances in DFIGs, leading to torque ripple, increased losses, and degraded efficiency with nonlinear loads. To address these challenges, a Versoria function–based zero-attraction least mean adaptive control is used to suppress harmonic distortion and ensure smooth autonomous operation. Proposed control enables seamless mode transitions and transient-free DFIG disconnection and reconnection. Real-time experimental validation confirms robust synchronization, enhanced power quality, and reliable performance under dynamic source and load variations.

item.title: A Hybrid Interpretable Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robust Pitch Control of Large-Scale Wind Turbines
item.description: The increasing size and structural flexibility of offshore wind turbines (WTs) give rise to complex multi-modal dynamics and strong aeroelastic coupling, which render accurate control-oriented modelling impractical for large-scale turbines. While deep reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising model-free alternative for pitch control, its application to large WTs remains challenged by training stability, safety, and limited interpretability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a model-free, safety-oriented, and interpretable RL-based pitch control framework for large-scale WTs. A hybrid architecture is developed by embedding a gain-scheduled PI (GSPI) baseline within a residual RL structure, together with a smooth damping mechanism to ensure stable learning. In addition, a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based module is incorporated to interpret the learned policy through feature importance and time-resolved control patterns. Simulation results in OpenFAST using a 15 MW monopile WT demonstrate over 23% reductions in generator speed and power fluctuations under the nominal training scenario, together with mitigated tower and blade fatigue loads. Additional robustness evaluations under high-turbulence operating conditions further confirm that the proposed method maintains strong performance relative to the benchmark, and support safe, robust, and interpretable pitch control for large-scale WTs.

item.title: EMT-EMT Co-Simulation for Large-Scale Offshore Wind Integration in the New York State Grid
item.description: The rapid integration of large-scale offshore wind (OSW) farms and inverter-based resources (IBRs) presents unprecedented challenges for power system stability and protection. While electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation provides the necessary fidelity to capture fast control interactions, modeling an entire regional grid alongside detailed OSW models exceeds the computational capacity of single real-time simulators. This paper presents the practical design, implementation, and validation of a distributed real-time EMT–EMT co-simulation framework to evaluate the integration of 9 GW of offshore wind into the New York State (NYS) power grid. By interfacing heterogeneous real-time simulators of RTDS and OPAL-RT via an Aurora-based fiber-optic communication link and a Transmission Line Model (TLM), the computational burden is effectively distributed. A comprehensive experimental evaluation is conducted, including a direct comparison between analog and fiber-optic interconnections. The results demonstrate that the Aurora-based fiber interface significantly improves latency, synchronization accuracy, and transient waveform fidelity compared to traditional analog setups. Ultimately, this application study demonstrates how the proposed framework overcomes the limitations of traditional interfaces, enabling high-fidelity, real-time stability assessment of the NYS grid under severe fault conditions and providing actionable insights to de-risk large-scale OSW deployment.

item.title: Knowledge-Data-Driven-Based Feasible Region of Frequency Regulation Parameter for Wind Farm
item.description: This letter proposes a knowledge-data-driven method for evaluating the feasible region of frequency regulation (FR) parameters in wind turbine generator (WTG). To this end, the system frequency model is firstly developed by integrating aerodynamics of WTG and FR. Then, the maximum frequency deviation is derived to quantify the FR capability requirement, which is the lower limitation for the feasible region. After that, a data-driven approach is used to quantitatively analyze the FR capability of WTG considering the rotor speed constraint, which is the upper limitation of the feasible region. Finally, a simulation model integrated with wind power is built in MATLAB/Simulink. The simulation results show that the proposed knowledge- data-driven method can accurately characterize the feasible region of FR parameter for WTG.

item.title: A Quantum-Assisted Boltzmann Machine for Wind Power Probabilistic Learning
item.description: Accurate probabilistic modeling of renewable power is essential for the secure operation and control of modern power systems. However, learning and modeling the data structure with high accuracy remains challenging due to the inherent spatial-temporal correlations of renewables. To address this issue, we propose a novel quantum-assisted Gaussian-Bernoulli restricted Boltzmann machine (GBRBM), which is intrinsically suitable for continuous wind power modeling. Furthermore, we tailor its negative phase to be directly solvable by quantum computing, thereby accelerating the learning process. Experiments conducted on real quantum hardware validate the cost-effective performance of the proposed method.

item.title: Transient Stability Analysis of Islanded Microgrid With Parallel Grid-Forming Converters Considering Current Limitation
item.description: To protect grid-forming (GFM) converters from overcurrent damage, current-limiting strategies are typically employed. However, such strategies may compromise the safe and stable operation of islanded microgrids during load restoration. To address this issue, this paper investigates the transient stability of an islanded microgrid with two parallel GFMs and analyzes the evolution of the GFMs’ dynamic behavior after a constant-impedance load is connected. First, a transient mathematical model of the system is developed considering current limiting. Then, since the output power of GFMs varies with their operating modes, significantly affecting the system’s transient stability, a method is proposed to determine both the mode-switching conditions and the final operating mode of each GFM solely within the first swing. On this basis, a hybrid approach combining numerical integration and the equal-area criterion is employed to accurately evaluate the transient stability. Furthermore, the proposed framework is applied to parameter tuning and short-circuit fault analysis in islanded microgrids. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation results.

item.title: Thermal-Mechanical Unified Inertia Estimation and Enhancement of Free Piston Stirling Generator in Island Microgrid
item.description: Compared with power electronic converter and diesel generator, the free piston Stirling generator (FPSG) with maintenance-free features has many advantages such as large overcurrent capability, high reliability, and wide heat source adaptability, as well as providing voltage and frequency references. Therefore, FPSG is a powerful competitor in supplying power to island microgrids and providing inertia to resist disturbance. However, unlike rotating devices, FPSG is a thermal-mechanical coupled system, and the two sets of vibrating components are subjected to approximate sinusoidal harmonic vibration, which poses difficulties for inertia analysis. To fill this gap, this paper provides a method for accurately calculating the frequency and power response during the dynamic process, which is the core of inertia analysis. Subsequently, a unified thermal-mechanical inertia estimation method that considers both the frequency reduction to provide mechanical power and the displacement of pistons increase to convert more thermal power is proposed. Then, the inertia enhancement method is provided, which effectively increases the frequency nadir and transition time. Finally, the proposed inertia estimation and enhancement method is verified through simulation and experiment.

item.title: Two-Stage Risk-Based Scheduling for Electricity–Biogas Rural Microgrids With Biomass Fermentation
item.description: Electricity-biogas rural microgrids (EBRMs) possess significant economic potential and the ability to coordinate multiple energy sources, making them a promising paradigm for energy management in rural areas. This paper proposes an energy scheduling method for an EBRM that utilizes renewable and biomass resources, with the goal of economically meeting rural electricity demand. The biogas fermentation process is modeled as a nonlinear biochemical dynamic system, where biogas production is governed by differential equations involving fermentation temperature and total solids (TS) concentration. A practical biogas fermentation model, which considers the dynamics of temperature and TS, is developed and subsequently linearized using McCormick relaxation. To more effectively capture renewable energy uncertainties beyond the tail focus of Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), a Gini-weighted CVaR (GWCVaR) model is introduced to quantify the risk of load shedding, formulating a stochastic mixed-integer programming problem. To address the mismatch between long-term biogas scheduling and day-ahead microgrid dispatch, a two-stage optimization strategy is proposed. Finally, simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness. The proposed method achieves a 26.2% reduction in operating cost compared to a baseline without biogas integration, while the integrated GWCVaR reduces load-shedding risk by over 85% with only a 3.4% cost penalty.

item.title: Autonomous Fixed-Time Model Predictive Control for Decentralized Coordination and Stabilization of Hybrid Fuel Cell/Battery/Supercapacitor Systems
item.description: For the fuel cell/battery/supercapacitor hybrid energy storage system (HESS) with constant power loads (CPLs), its controller needs to meet desired control goals, including decentralized dynamic power sharing, fast voltage regulation, large signal stabilization, reliability, and scalability. To this end, this paper proposes an autonomous fixed-time model predictive control (FxTMPC), which aims to achieve the above objectives with less system prior knowledge and sampling cost. First, the fixed-time disturbance observer (FxTDO) is constructed to estimate and feed-forward compensate for unknown and time-varying source-load side information, which not only reduces controller design complexity but also significantly improves robustness against disturbances. Second, the receding horizon optimization problem is solved offline based on source-load estimation variables, and FxTMPC is obtained by embedding fixed-time algorithms into the framework to correct the reference trajectory. Then, a decentralized hybrid droop control (DHDC) based on FxTMPC is developed, which achieves virtual impedance/resistance/capacitance at output terminals by modifying voltage reference values, not only enables different types of sources to respond to low/mid/high-frequency components of the load respectively, but also to reduce sensor usage with the assistance of FxTDO, thus achieving above the desired objectives with low cost. Finally, simulation and experimental results under multiple scenarios demonstrate that the proposed control strategy achieves HESS objectives with less prior knowledge and sensors, while comparative studies confirm its superiority.

item.title: Fixed-Time Privacy-Preserving Distributed Coordinated Control for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Inverters in Microgrids
item.description: As renewable energy integration continues to grow and microgrid (MG) systems become increasingly complex, it becomes critical to ensure system stability, security, and coordinated control among heterogeneous inverter types. This paper investigates the coordination among grid-forming inverters (GFMIs), grid-following inverters (GFLIs) under PQ control, and GFLIs under droop control. To address this problem, a communication layer based on the leader-follower consensus (LFC) architecture is established to enable information exchange among GFMIs, PQ-controlled GFLIs, and droop-controlled GFLIs. Building on this framework, a novel fixed-time privacy-preserving distributed coordinated controller is proposed by introducing a state decomposition mechanism. The proposed controller achieves fixed-time regulation of GFMI frequency and MG main bus voltage, ensures proportional active and reactive power sharing among all inverter types, and maintains the confidentiality of MG operational data. In comparison with existing studies, this work integrates the coordination of different inverter types, ensuring both operational efficiency and privacy protection, which has not been fully addressed in previous literature. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through real-time hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

item.title: Distributed-Centralized and Fully Distributed Secondary Control for Voltage Regulation and Current Sharing in DC Microgrid Clusters
item.description: The paper investigates the voltage regulation and proportional current sharing issues in a DC microgrid (MG) cluster comprising multiple single-bus DC MGs. First, a detailed electrical model of the DC MG cluster is developed, systematically incorporating both intra-MG and inter-MG power flow dynamics. Then, two dynamic consensus-based secondary control algorithms are proposed for the DC MG clusters. Specifically, one is a distributed-centralized control algorithm, where all distributed generation units (DGs) within each MG are aggregated into an integrated DG. These integrated DGs collaboratively generate control signals through distributed coordination and then broadcast them to the corresponding local DGs. The other is a fully distributed secondary control algorithm, capable of avoiding single-point failures. In this algorithm, a designated DG in each MG employs a distributed dynamic average consensus algorithm to ensure inter-MG voltage regulation and proportional current sharing, while the remaining DGs implement a local distributed control algorithm to achieve intra-MG proportional current sharing. The proposed secondary control algorithms are estimator-free, inherently avoiding constraints from precise estimator state initialization and facilitating the controller implementation. Furthermore, these algorithms are also applicable to both single-bus and multi-bus MGs. Finally, several simulations and experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

item.title: Situationally Aware Rolling Horizon Multi-Tier Load Restoration Considering Behind-the-Meter DER
item.description: Restoration in power distribution systems (PDSs) is well studied, however, most existing research focuses on network partition and microgrid formation, where load transfer is limited to adjacent feeders. This focus is not practical, as when adjacent feeders lack sufficient capacity, utilities may request support from more distant feeders in practice. Such a hierarchical restoration is complex, especially when involving changing system conditions due to cold load pickup and delayed reconnection of behind-the-meter DERs. To fill this research gap, a situationally aware multi-tier load restoration framework is proposed. Specifically, models are proposed to describe the multi-tier load restoration, including the multi-tier load transfer and substation transformer and feeder protection models. By introducing binary actional switching variables and load block transfer variables, the models effectively captures the dynamics of switches and multi-tier transfer process. To integrate situational awareness of evolving system conditions, the problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and then embedded within a rolling horizon optimization. Particularly, a set of safeguarded constraints are developed based on segment-level restoration reward bounds to mitigate the myopia of traditional rolling horizon optimization. The proposed safeguarded rolling strategy guarantees that each time step is lower bounded by a $(1-\varepsilon)$ -fraction of its optimal restoration potential, thereby balancing short-term switching decisions with long-term restoration goals. Finally, cases studies on the modified IEEE 123-node test feeder validate the proposed multi-tier restoration framework.

item.title: Hierarchically Coordinated Uncertainty Mitigation of Multi-Microgrids in Distribution Network
item.description: The proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) introduces significant uncertainties into distribution networks (DNs), threatening operational security. Concurrently, low-voltage DNs (LVDNs) interconnected via voltage source converters (VSCs) can form microgrid clusters (MCs), effec-tively mitigating voltage violations and load imbalances. To address the propagation of these multi-source uncertainties, this paper proposes a novel hierarchically coordinated operation framework for the DN and MCs. Within this framework, the MC layer manages localized uncertainty absorption and energy management, while the DN layer globally accommodates residual uncertainties and safeguards the overall system security based on the outcomes of MCs. Leveraging an online battery energy storage system (BESS) response strategy, a two-stage distributionally robust chance-constrained optimization (DRCO) model is established to co-optimize the day-ahead operational baselines and real-time mitigation factors. Chance constraints are formulated to jointly ensure BESS operational feasibility and network security, balancing robustness with mitigation efficiency. A computationally efficient solution methodology is further developed, which integrates chance constraint transformation with strong duality theory to reformulate the model into a tractable form. Simulations on a modified IEEE 123-bus DN with 8 MCs validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach in enhancing security, improving economics and mitigating uncertainty impacts.

item.title: Coordinated Load Frequency Control for Multi-Frequency Oscillations in Wind-Pumped Storage Hybrid Microgrids
item.description: Hybrid microgrids (MGs), particularly those incorporating wind power and pumped storage, have been widely adopted for renewable energy generation. However, hydraulic characteristics of pumped storage units (PSUs) and inter-generator interactions induce inevitably multi-frequency oscillations during load frequency control (LFC). To capture these oscillation behaviors and achieve effective suppression, this paper proposes a coordinated LFC strategy for hybrid MGs that integrates high-fidelity system modeling. A novel distributed frequency response (DFR) model is developed that incorporates hydraulic states (e.g., pressure heads in complicated pipelines and surge tank water levels) and network topology, offering improved accuracy over conventional average system frequency (ASF) models. Based on this model, a multi-input multi-output model predictive control (MIMO-MPC) scheme is designed to track the power allocation setpoint and enable wind turbines to participate in LFC in coordination with synchronous generators. Simulation results on 6-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems demonstrate the proposed strategy’s superiority in frequency regulation. Under variable wind conditions, it reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of frequency deviation for the PSU by 47.3% compared to the PI control. These outcomes validate the enhanced transient performance and robustness of the scheme for practical smart grid applications.

item.title: Risk-Aware Economic Scheduling for Hydrogen-Enabled Building Energy Systems Considering Extreme Weather Events
item.description: Hydrogen-enabled multi-energy systems (HMESs) have received much attention due to their low carbon emissions, high cross-sectoral/temporal/spatial flexibility, and black-start capability. However, their management under extreme weather events is particularly challenging due to the interacting multi-timescale dynamics of electrical-thermal-hydrogen subsystems, spatiotemporally coupled constraints, and large-scale mixed-integer decision variables. In this paper, we investigate a risk-aware economic scheduling problem for building-scale HMESs and aim to address all the above challenges. Specifically, by taking multi-timescale energy-coupled dynamics, extreme weather-induced source-load impacts, priority-based load shedding, and mobile emergency energy resources (e.g., electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles) into consideration, we formulate a risk-aware economic scheduling problem with the aim of minimizing the weighted sum of expected operation cost and conditional value-at-risk by optimizing the ex-ante rental quantities of mobile emergency energy resources. To solve this large-scale mixed-integer programming problem, we propose an algorithm that combines a farthest-first traversal-based clustering method with an improved quantum-behaved particle swarm optimizer (QBPSO)-based decomposition method. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

item.title: Decentralized Coordination of Household Energy Flexibility in Virtual Power Plants
item.description: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) and electric vehicles in residential sectors presents both challenges and opportunities for power system operators. Virtual power plants (VPPs) provide an effective mechanism to aggregate household flexibility and participate in electricity markets. This paper proposes a decentralized optimization framework for coordinating household flexibility within a VPP. Transformer-based non-intrusive load monitoring is applied to smart-meter data to recover appliance-level baselines, quantify flexibility, and estimate renewable generation. Building on these estimates, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-based algorithm is used to coordinate household scheduling with VPP-level participation in day-ahead, real-time, and ancillary service markets. The operator exchanges only aggregate signals and flexibility offers, while device-level decisions remain local, preserving privacy and enabling parallelism to improve computational efficiency and coordination responsiveness. Numerical studies on a real residential dataset under seasonal scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach, showing competitive market performance with fast convergence at portfolio scale.

item.title: Data-Driven Modeling of High-Resolution Residential Load Profiles Using Low-Resolution Smart Meter Measurements
item.description: Accurate and high-resolution residential load profiles are essential for power system modeling, demand response planning, and effective grid operation. As the energy sector moves towards a more actively managed distribution system, the ability to understand residential energy consumption at a minute-by-minute scale becomes increasingly critical. High-resolution load profiles provide key insights into demand patterns and user behavior, enabling grid operators to design more effective energy solutions; however, residential load measurements in the field are typically recorded at low resolutions, such as 15-60 minutes, which makes it hard to study the characteristics of different residential customers. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a data-driven approach to generate realistic, high-resolution residential load profiles based on low-resolution measurements and weather information. The proposed method retains the key features of the actual residential load measurements while offering appliance-level energy consumption details for each residential building. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed load profile generator, proving its capability to support utilities in optimizing residential energy management and ensuring a more reliable and resilient grid.

item.title: Multi-Time Scale Distributed Stochastic Economic Dispatch for Flexible Traction Power Supply System
item.description: Flexible traction power supply system (FTPSS), integrated with renewable energy, energy storage, and power flow controllers (PFC), offers great potential for safe and economical railway operation. However, the uncertainty in traction load and photovoltaic (PV) output poses significant challenges to cost-effective dispatch. Therefore, a multi-time scale distributed stochastic economic dispatch method for FTPSS is proposed. The prediction module uses LSTM to produce point forecasts, while KDE models the forecast errors to construct predictive intervals and generate scenarios for PV output and traction load. A stochastic programming model is then formulated, where uncertainties in traction load and PV are represented by chance constraints and scenarios. In the first stage, the day-ahead forecast is used to solve the stochastic optimization model to minimize daily operational cost.
