In the second stage, the scheduler uses the day-ahead plan as a soft reference and re-optimizes at each rolling step with updated probabilistic forecasts, implementing only the first control move to maintain real-time responsiveness and economic efficiency. The optimization model is solved using an ADMM-based distributed algorithm, which accounts for limited inter-subsystem communication and reduces computational complexity. A case study based on a real electrified railway demonstrates that the proposed method improves economic performance by reducing operating costs by approximately 9% under uncertainty.

item.title: Nodal Frequency Nadir Chance-Constrained Economic Dispatch Considering Contingency Frequency Service From Hydrogen Electrolysis
item.description: Providing contingency frequency services (CFSs) through grid-forming (GFM) converter-interfaced resources (CIRs) is a technically effective method for bolstering the frequency stability of low-inertia power systems. However, this approach often causes significant power curtailment or high capital investment. Moreover, the heterogeneous dynamic characteristics of CIRs and increasing uncertainty of renewable energy sources (RESs) renders system-level frequency metrics under deterministic conditions insufficient, necessitating the incorporation of uncertain nodal frequency nadir (NFN) to ensure comprehensive frequency stability. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a novel NFN chance-constrained economic dispatch framework, which leverages hydrogen electrolysis systems (HESs) as cost-effective sources of CFSs. The framework first establishes a synergistic operation strategy for integrated grid-following RESs and GFM HESs to enable efficient delivery of CFSs under stochastic contingencies. System-level power dispatch decisions and device-level CIR settings (i.e., control mode) are then co-optimized to minimize operation costs while ensuring both the system-level and node-level frequency stability. Finally, to overcome the computational burden of the nonlinear NFN chance constraints, a computationally tractable solution methodology is developed that leverages input convex neural networks with analytical sensitivity analysis and Benders decomposition methods. The effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach are validated through numerical simulations on two test systems.

item.title: Unified Model Aggregation of Active Distribution Network With Heterogeneous Uncertain Distributed Energy Resources
item.description: This paper proposes a unified aggregated model of active distribution network (ADN), which aggregates the whole ADN as an equivalent generator/adjustable load with exchange limits considering heterogeneous uncertain distributed energy resources. A min-max bi-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problem is built to check the disaggregation feasibility with given exchange limits. The network-constrained ADN model with DERs’ 0-1 operation status and uncertainties is built, where the adjustable robust optimization is adopted to handle uncertainties. To solve this problem, surrogate Lagrangian relaxation is used to relax the MILP problem into the bi-level linear programming (LP), which is further dualized to obtain a single-level MILP via the strong duality theory. We prove that the primal problem and the dual of its relaxed formulation share the same strong duality property. After the bi-level problem is solved, the initial infeasible dispatch command of all timeslots is obtained. Then, an iterative framework is proposed to adjust the aggregation exchange limits by analyzing the infeasible command and re-solving the bi-level problem. The iteration converges until all feasible commands of all timeslots are obtained. The proposed method is tested on IEEE-18 and IEEE-85 systems. Numerical results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in handling 0-1 operation status and ensuring robustness.

item.title: Power Management and Control for Flexible Traction Substation in Railway Hub Integrated With ESS, PV, and EV
item.description: It is promising to integrate the energy storage system (ESS), photovoltaic (PV), and electric vehicles (EVs) into the railway hub to achieve a flexible traction substation (FTSS) for decarbonizing the energy supply and enhancing the energy efficiency. However, the FTSS performance heavily depends on power flow management and control under complex and dynamic operating conditions. To address this issue, a centralized power flow control strategy synthesizing a joint active and reactive power management strategy (PMS) and a master-slave-based converter control strategy is proposed. The proposed PMS is executed in a central controller to determine the real-time power commands for converters by employing a joint active and reactive power command generation algorithm. Specifically, a two-stage linear optimization problem is formulated to optimize active power commands so that the utilization of regenerative braking energy (RBE) and PV energy can be maximized. Subsequently, reactive power commands are calculated based on the residual converter capacities to improve the power quality of the traction power system and railway distribution system. Based on the power commands from the central controller, the master-slave control coordinates the local controllers of converters for power flow control. The efficacy and superiority of the proposed method are demonstrated through experiment and field load data-based evaluation and comparison. Besides, the implementation of the proposed method is discussed from the energy trading mechanism and application scenario.

item.title: B-DRNet: A Stereo Vision-Based Framework for Safety Distance Monitoring in Substations
item.description: Monitoring the safety distance between maintenance personnel and live components is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the intelligent power grid. To address this issue, this study proposes a distance measurement framework, B-DRNet, which integrates keypoint detection with binocular stereo perception. The method constructs an innovative detector architecture incorporating three improvements: hierarchical feature aggregation block (HFAB), multi-scale attention hypergraph (MSAH), and a decoupled detection head (DDH), which significantly enhance feature representation capability and improve the detection accuracy of small objects. Meanwhile, a stereo perception module based on GwcNet is employed to obtain dense depth information, and coordinate mapping is utilized to achieve three-dimensional distance measurement. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed detector outperforms existing models in both detection performance and operational efficiency, with AP improved by 6.68%, frame rate reaching 333 f/s, and parameter size reduced to 1.05 M. The average distance measurement error is 3.18%, which meets practical application requirements and fully verifies its practicality and reliability in substation safety monitoring. B-DRNet achieves a favorable balance among detection accuracy, operational efficiency, and ranging reliability, enabling stable and accurate three-dimensional safety-distance monitoring in complex substation scenarios and providing an efficient solution for automated safety monitoring in substations.

item.title: PI-YOLO: An Efficient Detector for Power Line Inspection Using Aerial Images
item.description: Power line inspection, as a critical task of smart grid maintenance, has been empowered by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and neural detectors for automation and intelligence. The inspection task requires detectors to identify diverse equipment in high-resolution aerial images rapidly and accurately. However, existing detectors are still insufficient to meet these requirements, primarily due to their inadequate dataset scale, high-resolution adaptability, and network efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper first collects 99202 inspection images with a resolution of $4939\times 2987$ and annotates 52 categories, thereby establishing the Power Inspection Unify Dataset (PIUD) as the data foundation. Then, PIUD is further processed by the proposed Power Inspection Multi-Scale (PIMS) framework to PIUD-MS to support high-resolution training and inference. Finally, this paper develops PI-YOLO based on YOLOv11 with improved performance in terms of multi-scale capability, network structure, and receptive field. PI-YOLO is publicly released as an efficient detector for inspection or annotation applications, whose advanced performance is validated by experiments on COCO, PIUD-MS, and InsPLAD. Compared with the baseline YOLOv11 and other detectors, PI-YOLO achieves both performance improvement and latency reduction. For example, PI-YOLO-Large improves AP by 0.7 while reducing latency by 1ms on PIUD-MS compared to YOLOv11.

item.title: Adaptive Fast Clearing Algorithm-Based Peer-to-Peer Transaction for Microgrid-Integrated Distribution Network Considering Uncertainty
item.description: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction has become an effective way to improve the economic efficiency of microgrids (MGs). However, existing studies neglect the impacts of electricity power-carbon-green certificate join cost (PCGC), energy-reserve co-optimization and uncertainty within MG on P2P transactions schemes. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a P2P transaction framework for interconnected MG, where carbon allowance-green certificate constraints, reserve constraints, joint chance constraints are employed respectively to capture PCGC coupling, reserve provisioning, and uncertainty impacts. An optimization-based piecewise-linear marginal utility function (MUF) is developed to characterize MG’s price-responsive behaviors under multi-resource coordination. Furthermore, an adaptive fast clearing algorithm (AFCA) is designed with a network-fee-exempt non-iterative clearing scheme and a network-fee-incorporated oscillation-resistant iterative scheme to ensure computational efficiency and distribution network security. Numerical results demonstrate that the MUF effectively captures the impacts of internal reserve, network constraints, risk preference, and PCGC on inter-MG P2P trading behaviors. The AFCA significantly accelerates computation, with a 97.72% time reduction compared to the widely used alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) in a 5-MG system, and solves the 20-MG system in only 1.45 s with an optimality error of merely 0.59%.

item.title: Real-Time Charging Control for Electric Roadways
item.description: This paper studies the optimal wireless charging for electric vehicles (EVs) driving through an electric roadway (ER). We first develop a clairvoyant formulation to model and optimize the minute-level energy transmission between the ER and EVs, which incorporates ER microgrid operation, EV-side power balance, battery dynamics, and wireless power transfer limits as constraints. However, this formulation requires future information regarding how EVs will be driven, which is often unavailable during real-time operation. To circumvent the dependence on future information, we design a causal algorithm by leveraging the optimality of valley-filling charging profiles of the clairvoyant formulation. We theoretically establish the optimality of the proposed algorithm in an ideal setting without considering losses. The algorithm is then extended to account for practicalities such as estimation errors, losses, and incorporation of a stationary battery co-located with the ER. Finally, for distinct traffic conditions, we numerically validate the performance of the algorithm under realistic settings (incorporating losses) with different information patterns (with and without lookahead).

item.title: Time-Efficient and Tractable DRCC-Based Optimal Operation of EV Charging Stations Under Uncertainty
item.description: With the growing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs), efficient and robust operation of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) has become increasingly important. This article proposes an optimal scheduling problem for multiple EVCSs, while considering uncertainties in individual EVs’ forecasted arrival/departure times and desired energy demands. To address this, a distributionally robust chance-constraint (DRCC)-based optimization framework is proposed, which utilizes a Wasserstein distance-based ambiguity set. Considering the above EV uncer-tainty parameters, a general DRCC formulation for EVCS-level constraints is difficult to achieve. The proposed optimization framework maps the above EV uncertainty parameters into a single uncertainty parameter of EVCS total charging power, thereby enabling a general DRCC formulation. In addition, EV constraints are formulated to allow arrival/departure times to be treated as continuous rather than discrete time intervals. We also propose a time efficient DRCC reformulation method that considers the physical limits of the uncertainty parameter. Case studies based on real-world EVCS data are conducted to validate the operational efficiency and robustness of the proposed method for multiple EVCSs.

item.title: Dynamic Programming-Based Non-Anticipative Approach for Multi-Stage Coordinated Optimal Dispatch of Electricity and Transportation Nexus
item.description: This paper proposes a coordinated dispatch approach for integrated power distribution network (PDN) and urban traffic network (UTN), which is a pioneering effort to simultaneously optimize day-ahead strategies and real-time decision policies for PDN dispatch and UTN traffic assignment. The methodology utilizes a dynamic programming model within a multi-stage robust optimization framework, enabling comprehensive optimization across diverse time horizons via cascaded cost-to-go functions. A tractable dynamic traffic flow model is incorporated to characterize electric vehicle (EV) operations over short time intervals. Furthermore, vehicle-to-grid (V2G) services are considered to augment the system’s operational flexibility. Leveraging the proposed multi-stage framework, the proposed dispatch model effectively addresses uncertainties with non-anticipative constraints, which is usually ignored in existing studies. Besides, a dimension-aware improved robust dual dynamic programming algorithm is developed to solve this model. The effectiveness of the proposed model and its solution methodology is validated through comprehensive case studies on a 33-bus PDN with a 20-road UTN and a larger-scale, real-world 91-bus PDN with a 35-road UTN.

item.title: Data-Driven Privacy-Preserving Modeling and Frequency Regulation With Aggregated Electric Vehicles via Bilinear Hidden Markov Model
item.description: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology allows bidirectional power flow for real-time grid support, making electric vehicles (EVs) well-suited for ancillary services such as frequency regulation. However, existing methods for flexibility estimation and coordinating aggregated EVs often rely on individual EV traveling information (e.g., arrival/departure time) and/or characteristic parameters (e.g., charging efficiency, battery capacity) as well as real-time state-of-charge (SOC), which raises privacy concerns and faces data quality issues. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a data-driven, privacy-preserving modeling and control framework for frequency regulation using aggregated EVs. The proposed method can provide accurate estimation for power outputs and flexibility of aggregated EVs and carry out effective frequency regulation without any individual EV information. Simulation results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method, which also outperforms the model-based and federated learning-based method under SOC data inaccuracies.

item.title: Sharding-Based Asynchronous Coordination for Secure and Scalable Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Under Delays and Attacks
item.description: The proliferation of distributed energy resources has enabled the emergence of prosumers and peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. However, many existing decentralized market clearing schemes that require iterative message exchanges are vulnerable to false data injection (FDI) and can stall under heterogeneous communication delays. Blockchain solutions enhance integrity but often rely on synchronous optimization and global consensus, yielding excessive overhead. In this paper, a sharding-based asynchronous coordination mechanism for network-constrained P2P energy trading is developed. First, an asynchronous decentralized optimization method is developed to clear the market with respect to network constraints. Second, a dynamic sharding method is proposed to partition prosumers into low-latency shards by jointly considering trading relationships and communication delays, thereby localizing coordination and reducing cross-network synchronization. Third, a lightweight consensus mechanism that integrates asynchronous updates with a chained verification structure is designed to verify message correctness and detect malicious behaviors, thereby enabling fast intrashard agreement without the need for global synchronous rounds. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach preserves scalability and reduces the overall runtime by 79.15% compared with benchmark mechanisms while maintaining secure clearing performance under attack scenarios.

item.title: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning With Expert Workflow for Real-Time P2P Energy Trading
item.description: Real-time peer-to-peer (P2P) electricity markets dynamically adapt to fluctuations in renewable energy and variations in demand, maximizing economic benefits through instantaneous price responses while enhancing grid flexibility. However, scaling expert guidance for massive personalized prosumers poses critical challenges, including diverse decision-making demands and a lack of customized modeling frameworks. This paper proposes an integrated large language model-multi-agent reinforcement learning (LLM-MARL) framework for real-time P2P energy trading to address challenges such as the limited technical capability of prosumers, the lack of expert experience, and security issues of distribution networks. LLMs are introduced as experts to generate personalized strategies, guiding MARL under the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm through imitation. To handle the scalability issues inherent in large-scale P2P networks, a differential attention-based critic network is introduced to efficiently extract key interaction features and enhance convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that LLM-generated strategies effectively substitute human experts. The proposed imitative expert MARL algorithms achieve significantly lower economic costs and voltage violation rates on test sets compared to baseline algorithms, while maintaining robust stability. This paper provides an effective solution for the real-time decision-making of the P2P electricity market by bridging expert knowledge with agent learning.

item.title: Large Language Model-Based Smart Agents for Attack-Defense Game on Cyber-Physical Power Systems
item.description: With the deep integration of information technology, cyber-physical power systems (CPPSs) face increasingly complex attack-defense challenges. Traditional game theory-based methods struggle with sophisticated strategy reasoning and decision interpretability. This paper proposes an innovative CPPS attack-defense game paradigm incorporating large language model (LLM)-based smart agents to address these limitations. First, we define a game model integrating Bayesian Nash Equilibrium and betweenness centrality to characterize the strategy stability and key node prioritization. Second, we design smart agent architectures with memory, toolset, planning, and action execution modules to enable adaptive strategy formulation in complex environments. Then, we give a systematic elaboration of the dynamic game processes, including vulnerability scanning, attack, detection, response, and post-analysis phases. Experiments on IEEE 14 and IEEE 33 bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances defense success rate, convergence efficiency, and strategy diversity, validating the potential of LLMs in improving CPPS security through the intelligent attack-defense game.

item.title: Tractable Attack Detection With Robustness Certificate for Nonlinear Power Systems Under Stochastic Disturbances
item.description: This article presents a tractable attack detection methodology for nonlinear power systems that reduces complexity while providing a formal certificate of robustness against stochastic power disturbances. The inherent nonlinearity of power system dynamics typically necessitates sophisticated detection algorithms, while stochastic disturbances (e.g., fluctuating renewables) may introduce unforeseen behaviors that obscure attack discernment. This leads to two primary challenges: (i) model-based methods offer strong analytical foundations but may suffer from high computational complexity and rely on prior assumptions about disturbance distributions (e.g., Gaussianity); (ii) data-driven methods address uncertainty using statistical properties of large datasets or empirical validation within neural network architectures, yet they may lack performance guarantees. To this end, we propose (i) a linear detector that encodes stochastic disturbances through quadratic constraints, transforming the robust design problem into a convex quadratic program (QP), thereby ensuring tractability, and (ii) a robustness certificate that provides probabilistic guarantees in unseen scenarios with a desired confidence, based on the behavior of the optimal solution in active constraints (i.e., constraints that are equalities at the optimum). Unlike existing methods, our detection approach leverages the optimality properties of convex optimization to deliver performance guarantees without depending on prior assumptions or large datasets. We validate our method on cyber attack detection in Automatic Generation Control (AGC) within a two-area IEEE 118-bus system.

item.title: Simplicial Graph-Based Detection and Localization of Cyber Attacks Against Large-Scale Smart Grids
item.description: Ensuring the resilience of large-scale power systems against cyber attacks is critical to maintaining the stability of modern cyber-physical energy systems. Existing machine learning (ML)-based detection frameworks predominantly focus on pairwise node interactions (i.e., edges) and often overlook capturing higher-order topological structures (i.e., simplicial complexes) that emerge within power networks. This paper introduces a novel simplicial recurrent graph neural network (SRGNN) for attack detection and localization in large-scale smart grid infrastructure. Unlike conventional graph models, SRGNN incorporates higher-order simplicial interactions to capture group-wise dependencies among buses and transmission lines, allowing the model to better reflect the multi-scale dynamics of grid operation and control. We investigate the robustness of our model against benchmark and proposed complex simplicial-based attack node selection strategies. Our extensive experiments on large-scale transmission power networks ( $2{,}869$ -bus, $9{,}241$ -bus, and $70{,}000$ -bus systems) demonstrate that the proposed SRGNN model outperforms ML-based benchmark models, achieving superior detection and localization performance by 9–39% and 8–35%, respectively, in detection rate against complex attacks. These results underscore the importance of modeling higher-order topological structures for robust and scalable security in power systems.

item.title: Quantal Response-Based Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Smart Grid Attack-Defense Game With Bounded Rationality Evolution
item.description: Smart grids enhance power transmission efficiency through integrated cyber-physical systems, but simultaneously increase vulnerability to unexpected contingencies and malicious attacks. Adversarial reinforcement learning (ARL) has emerged as a promising technique for grid attack-defense games, however, existing methods assume attackers’ complete rationality, forcing defenders to engage in complex saddle-point optimization problems (i.e., solving for worst-case Nash equilibrium). Such an issue not only leads to over-conservative defenders, but also poses severe convergence challenges. To mitigate these problems, this paper proposes a novel quantal response-based ARL (QR-ARL) method. QR-ARL generalizes ARL into bounded rationality via entropy regularization, which helps reflect realistic attacker behaviors and reduce defensive conservatism. Building on this, a novel self-paced learning technique is then tailored to manage training complexity by adaptively evolving the attacker’s rationality. Additionally, to address the potential conflict between short-term control costs and long-term stability objectives, a parameter space perturbation technique is proposed to promote exploration and reduce the agent’s reliance on local reward signals. Numerical experiments on IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus systems confirm the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method over existing ARL methods.

item.title: An Autonomous Identification and Mitigation Scheme for Man-in-the-Middle Attacks on Microgrid Secondary Control Signals
item.description: In centralized microgrids, secondary control signals are transmitted from the microgrid central controller (MGCC) to each distributed energy resource (DER) to restore voltage and frequency. However, these signals remain vulnerable to cyber attacks. Unlike unidirectional attacks, such as false data injection and denial-of-service attacks, Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks enable bidirectional manipulation of both uplink and downlink communications, making detection and mitigation at the MGCC extremely challenging. To address these practical challenges, a novel autonomous identification and mitigation scheme is proposed in this paper for centralized microgrids, utilizing only the local measurements from each DER. In this scheme, each DER independently determines whether it is under attack by analyzing the trajectories of local measurements and calculated values at the point of common coupling. The attack signals are then reconstructed with the attack frequency and amplitude components estimated via Fast Fourier Transform and least squares estimation. Subsequently, the attacked DER implements mitigation actions by injecting the inverse of the reconstructed attack signals back into the local controller. Compared to existing schemes, the proposed scheme: 1) utilizes local measurements only, enhancing resilience against MITM attacks in centralized microgrids; 2) identifies specific attacked secondary control signals; and 3) reconstructs and mitigates complex attack waveforms without relying on additional trustworthy communication links. The proposed scheme is evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink, with simulations confirming its effectiveness in identifying and mitigating MITM attacks.

item.title: Entropy-Regularized Weighted Federated Meta-Learning Approach for Power Load Forecasting in Non-IID Scenarios
item.description: Accurate power load forecasting is crucial for smart grid security and efficiency, yet traditional centralized methods fall short in addressing data privacy and communication demands. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising solution but faces dual challenges: the Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) nature of load data limits model generalization and invites security threats like model poisoning attacks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Federated Meta-Learning (FedML) framework integrated with Entropy-Regularized Gradient-Weighted (ER-Grad) aggregation. The framework employs FedML to construct high-precision personalized forecasting models for clients while maintaining training efficiency, thereby significantly enhancing predictive performance. Additionally, the ER-Grad aggregation algorithm is introduced to dynamically calibrate client weights, effectively suppressing abnormal or malicious updates and strengthening the system’s robustness against model poisoning attacks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially improves overall and peak forecasting accuracy, ensures comprehensive robustness against malicious attacks and communication dropouts, and achieves training with high efficiency.

item.title: Cyberattack Detection in Line Current Differential Relays via Transient Circuit Model-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: With the digital transformation of power systems, Line Current Differential Relays (LCDRs) are facing increasingly severe cybersecurity risks. Existing cyberattack detection methods are usually reliant on known attack models or additional measurement techniques, which limit their reliability and practicality. To address these issues, a cyberattack detection method based on line parameter consistency is proposed. A Cyberattack Detection Metric (CDM) is presented in terms of the consistency of line parameters during faults. A Transient Circuit Model-Informed Neural Network (TCINN) is developed to identify line parameters during transient processes. The TCINN is integrated with a physics-inspired filter and fault model-based physical constraints, allowing accurate parameter identification with only limited fault samples and a simplified transmission line model. The identified parameters are incorporated into the CDM to enable attacks detection. Proposed method can detect coordinated false data injection attacks (C-FDIAs) that simultaneously target local measurements and communicated currents, and is also applicable to false data injection attacks (FDIAs), replay attacks (RAs), and fault-masking attacks (FMAs) that target only communicated currents. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 99.9% under FDIA and RA attacks, 93.6% under C-FDIA, and 98.4% under FMA, thereby providing an effective solution for enhancing the cybersecurity of LCDRs.

item.title: Joint Cyber-Physical Data-Driven Enhanced Cyber-Attack Detection for Power Systems
item.description: Rapid, early, and accurate detection of cyber intrusions is increasingly vital for ensuring the security and operational resilience of modern power systems, as cyber-attacks grow in both frequency and sophistication. However, existing approaches primarily focus on either cyber or physical data independently, ignoring critical interactions across these two layers. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel Cross-Layer Graph Attention-Transformer Network (CL-GTN), which simultaneously incorporates information from both the cyber and physical layers, and effectively integrates them through a learnable physics-informed point-to-bus projection mechanism. Specifically, the projection matrix constructed from power system sensitivity factors explicitly captures the fine-grained mapping from cyber data points in communication packets to affected physical grid nodes, providing a robust cross-layer fusion basis. Graph attention networks (GAT) are employed separately at the cyber and physical layers to extract relevant local and topological features, followed by a Transformer module that dynamically aggregates cross-layer temporal dependencies for accurate attack identification. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark systems, including the IEEE 118-bus and large-scale ACTIVSg2000 systems, confirm that CL-GTN achieves high detection accuracy (over 0.98) and strong early-warning capability, successfully detecting up to 90% of attacks before execution with an average lead of 2.4 time steps. Comprehensive ablation and robustness studies further validate the model’s stability and component effectiveness. In addition, interpretability analyses show that the proposed projection-matrix mechanism accurately identifies critical cyber–physical coupling points, thereby enhancing situational awareness and defense capability.

item.title: Detection of Out-of-Distribution Power Quality Disturbance Using Dual-Channel Gramian Angular Field With Enhanced Mahalanobis Distance
item.description: Deep learning methods for the power quality disturbance (PQD) classification encounter significant deployment challenges in power system applications. With the increasing integration of renewable energy, electric vehicles, and other non-traditional loads, the out-of-distribution (OOD) data occurs frequently due to evolving power system conditions, which represents a critical yet underexplored challenge. In this study, the OOD problem in the PQD classification is formally defined, where models encounter the absence of disturbance patterns during training. Leveraging the unique characteristics of PQD data, a four-stage multimodal OOD detection method is developed for the OOD-driven framework to enhance PQD classification. The proposed method first transforms PQD waveforms into dual-channel Gramian Angular Field (GAF) maps, then extracts discriminative features with vision Transformers. Mahalanobis distance is employed for OOD scoring, and a multimodal auxiliary criterion is introduced to enhance the distinction between in-distribution (IND) and OOD. Comprehensive case studies are conducted using both simulated IEEE standard-compliant waveforms and practical PQD data. Results applied to the simulated PQD data demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve a 2.10% of false positive rate at 90% true positive recall (FPR90), outperforming all previous methods. Practical applications demonstrate a remarkable 9.64% improvement in the PQD classification accuracy compared to the unfiltered dataset containing OOD samples.

item.title: Surrogate Models in Power System Scheduling Problems: Learning Active Constraints via Graph Neural Networks
item.description: Power system scheduling problems are solved repeatedly and require fast computation for real time deployment of asset setpoints. Bilevel optimization is often employed due to its ability to capture the hierarchical structure between network operators and end users. However, the inherent complexity of bilevel models makes repeated solutions computationally expensive. To address this, we propose a surrogate modeling approach that predicts the set of active constraints in the full bilevel formulation, thereby significantly reducing computational effort. Rather than relying on extensive sampling over uncertain parameters, we exploit the bipartite graph structure of optimization problems and apply Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to learn constraint activity directly by leveraging the intrinsic geometric dependencies of the optimization models. We evaluate the end to end approach by comparing the surrogate objective values and computational speedup against the original problem, benchmarking against Random Forest (RF) and Feed-foward Neural Network (FNN) classifiers across a range of increasingly complex test cases, from linear programming problems to mixed integer linear programming and bilevel problems. Results show that GNN based models, which encode mathematical properties like complementary slackness and binary activations to reduce model complexity, achieve up to 10-20x speedup with an objective deviation under 4% and a 99% optimality ratio. This represents superior performance to RFs and FNN, highlighting the suitability of GNNs for directly encoding the mathematical structure of optimization models, thanks to its inherent topology awareness to solve complex constraint activity prediction tasks in power system scheduling.

item.title: Deep Multi-Modal Fusion and Kalman Online Adaptation for Electric Load Forecasting Against Extreme Rainfall Events
item.description: Extreme rainfall (ERF), one of the most frequent and widespread severe weather hazards, has significant impacts on power systems. The sudden and unpredictable nature of precipitation can cause abrupt changes in power consumption behavior, posing significant challenges for accurate electric load forecasting. Satellite images provide fine-grained spatial characteristics of weather phenomena, which can be leveraged to capture rainfall patterns and trajectories that influence power demand. To this end, this paper proposes a multimodal learning and online adaptation-based load forecasting method for ERF disasters by taking both satellite images and time series data as input. Instead of relying on convolutional neural networks or Transformers, a novel lightweight MLP-Mixer architecture is devised. It leverages three types of Mixer operations—time-mixing, token-mixing, and channel-mixing—to process sequential satellite images, which allows the proposed model to capture both local rainfall details and broader weather dynamics while ensuring lower computational costs. Following this, a gated multimodal unit is devised to adaptively fuse multimodal representations of images and numerical features by learning to decide how modalities influence the activation of the unit. To enable the model to rapidly adapt to load pattern changes caused by ERF events, a modified extended Kalman filter-based online adaptation algorithm is further developed to dynamically update model parameters using newly arrived load data. Extensive experiments on distribution network load data from ERF events show that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art load forecasting methods.

item.title: Robust Region of Attraction for DC Microgrids Under Uncertain Loading Conditions
item.description: A guaranteed region of attraction (ROA) is essential for ensuring transient stability in DC microgrids. Numerical methods and control strategies for ROA design often rely on parameter tuning tailored to a specific operating scenario. When the steady-state load varies, both the operating point and the associated ROA change, causing fixed-scenario guarantees to break down and offering limited robustness. This letter develops a robust control synthesis method that ensures transient stability with guaranteed ROA. First, a robust stability condition is proposed to ensure a guaranteed ROA that adaptively moves with the operating point; then, we incorporate the condition into an optimal power flow (OPF)-like control synthesis problem that jointly ensures operational feasibility and robust stability guarantees while preserving computational efficiency. Simulation case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: Online Stochastic Optimization for Coordinating EV Charging Stations With PV-Battery Systems
item.description: The surge in electric vehicle adoption strains charging stations (CSs) and the grid, calling for distributed resource integration and CS coordination to manage random supply and demand. This letter introduces a novel online stochastic optimization method that improves operation revenue and facilitates CS collaboration by ensuring the economic profitability of battery operations through a deterministic guarantee and setting battery-based prices. Simulations demonstrate near-optimal performance while upholding service quality and stability.

item.title: A General Distributed Bounded-and-Deadband Voltage Control Framework for Microgrids
item.description: This letter proposes a general distributed voltage control framework for microgrids capable of enforcing both voltage deadbands and bounds. A barrier-based state-mapping function is embedded into consensus-based controllers to confine the voltage trajectories of distributed energy resources within a predefined bound and avoid unnecessary control actions inside the deadband. In addition, some contingencies that exceed the setting bounds are also considered and discussed. The framework is simple in structure and can be adapted to any mapping function that meets the design criteria.

item.title: Unified Energy Consumption Modeling for Heterogeneous UAVs: An Adaptative Incremental Learning-Based Framework
item.description: Accurate energy consumption modeling is a prerequisite for reliable mission scheduling and network coverage in the low-altitude economy. However, the proliferation of heterogeneous Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) introduces significant challenges: existing models are typically platform-specific, failing to generalize across diverse aerodynamic structures, while retraining for every new UAV type is computationally prohibitive. To address these issues, we propose UECM-IL, an incremental learning-based framework that establishes a unified energy consumption model. First, to explicitly capture both the sequential evolution of flight states and the intrinsic dependencies among features, we develop a Knowledge Graph guided Temporal-Graph Network (KG-TGN). This dual-channel architecture utilizes a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to capture sequential flight dynamics and a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) guided by a domain-knowledge graph to model inter-feature correlations. Second, to enable cross-domain generalization without catastrophic forgetting, we introduce an incremental learning strategy termed Overfitting-aWare learning rate scheduling and Experience Replay (OWER). This mechanism allows the model to sequentially adapt to new aerial platforms while retaining historical domain knowledge. Finally, we construct the Multi-scenario Heterogeneous UAV Energy Consumption Dataset (MH-UECD), collected via the AirFogSim platform across five distinct aerodynamic configurations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the unified model achieves an average Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 2.0% across heterogeneous domains, offering a scalable solution for energy-aware low-altitude management.

item.title: Proximal Policy Optimization With Predictive and Memory-Aware Battery Management for BEVs Using Hybrid Energy Storage and Battery Health-Oriented Rewards
item.description: The increasing use of electric vehicles (EVs) calls for the development of sophisticated battery management strategies (BMSs) to maximize performance and lengthen the lifespan of components. Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) that make use of a single energy storage system (ESS) are electric vehicle architectures that necessitate rigorous energy management to guarantee efficiency and longevity. To improve energy utilization efficiency, hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) have been developed. These kinds of ESS combine super capacitors with batteries (SCs). Although HESS designs provide enhanced power handling and a longer driving range, they also add an additional layer of complexity to the design of BMSs. In this research, an intelligent BMS for BEVs equipped with a battery–supercapacitor as HESS is proposed. The proposed framework integrates a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning algorithm with a Convolutional Neural NetworkLong–Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) predictor to forecast future driving demands while considering historical patterns and the battery’s state of health (SOH). To optimize energy distribution and preserve battery health, the BMS makes use of multi-dimensional observations, such as the state of charge (SOC) of the battery, the SOH, the voltage of the SC, the speed of the vehicle, and the distance traveled. The proposed strategy demonstrates superior performance in both energy efficiency and battery health preservation when compared with state-of-the-art RLbased methods. Specifically, it reduces battery capacity fading by 2.38% and 1.12% relative to PPO and SAC without memory-aware mechanisms, as well as SAC with memory-aware features, while simultaneously achieving a higher final SOC than all benchmark counterparts.

item.title: STAR-RIS–Assisted UAV Communications for Dynamic Spectrum Sharing in NOMA Under Imperfect SIC: Enabling Cognitive Radio Networks
item.description: The simultaneous transmission and reflection of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) enhances the spectrum efficiency (SE) of primary users (PUs) and secondary users (SUs) in cognitive radio (CR) networks by mitigating interference from incident signals. The STAR-RIS-assisted unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can fully cover the environment due to its high mobility and fast deployment. According to the dynamic air-to-ground channels, the STAR-RIS-assisted UAV faces a challenge in determining the coefficient of the element’s role during flight. To meet the requirements of dynamic channel determination with the SE approach, this paper proposes the sum rate maximization of both PUs and SUs through non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in a CR network to jointly optimize the trajectory and transmission-reflection beamforming design of the STAR-RIS-assisted UAV, and power allocation under the imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). Since the non-convex joint optimization problem includes coupled variables, we develop an alternative optimization algorithm. Simulation results examine the impact of parameters on fixed and mobile users, evaluate the performance of intelligent surface modes and operating protocols, and highlight the advantages of adopted NOMA (under perfect/imperfect SIC) over OMA. The gap analysis confirms that our proposed dynamic system model numerically outperforms the benchmarks.

item.title: A Low-Complexity Zak-OTFS Receiver With Over-Sampling in the Delay-Doppler Domain
item.description: In this paper, we present a novel low-complexity receiver that performs detection and channel estimation tasks in Zak-OTFS modulation using over-sampling in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. Towards this, we partition the over-sampled signal into multiple two-dimensional (2D) blocks, which is equivalent to parallel branch conventional sampling of delay- and Doppler-shifted signals. This partitioning along with processing only a subset of the partitioned 2D blocks aids in reducing complexity. Specifically, in terms of detection, we propose a symbol-wise selection-based detection (SSD) algorithm which makes symbol-wise decisions based on selection among parallel branch outputs. While the partition based processing reduces complexity, the selection-based symbol decisions offer good performance. We also exploit the proposed partitioning for low-complexity path-wise estimation of the DD channel taps based on maximum energy across blocks. Simulation results with fractional DDs show that the proposed detection and channel estimation algorithms for Zak-OTFS achieve good performance at low complexity.

item.title: Coupler Position Optimization and Channel Estimation for Flexible Coupler Antenna Aided Multiuser Communication
item.description: In this paper, we propose a flexible coupler antenna (FCA), also referred to as a reconfigurable coupler antenna (RCA), to enhance wireless communication performance at low hardware cost. At each FCA, there is one fixed-position active antenna and multiple passive couplers that can move within a designated region around the active antenna. Moreover, each FCA is equipped with a local processing unit (LPU). All LPUs exchange signals with a central processing unit (CPU) for joint signal processing. We study an FCA-aided multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system, where an FCA array base station (BS) is deployed to enhance the downlink communication between the BS and multiple single-antenna users. We formulate optimization problems to maximize the achievable sum rate of users by jointly optimizing the coupler positions and digital beamforming, subject to movement constraints on the coupler positions and the transmit power constraint. To address the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, the digital beamforming is expressed as a function of the coupler position vectors, which are then optimized using the proposed distributed coupler position optimization algorithm. Considering a structured time domain pattern of pilots and coupler positions, pilot-assisted centralized and distributed channel estimation algorithms are designed under the FCA array architecture. Simulation results demonstrate that the distributed FCA array achieves substantial rate gains over conventional benchmarks in multiuser systems without moving active antennas, and approaches the performance of fully active arrays while significantly reducing hardware cost. Moreover, the proposed centralized channel estimation outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of both pilot overhead and channel reconstruction accuracy, while the distributed scheme provides a favorable accuracy and complexity tradeoff by shifting computations to the LPUs.

item.title: Sensing Performance Optimization for ISAC With ITS and IRS
item.description: In this paper, a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system architecture is introduced that incorporates an intelligent transmission surface (ITS) in the transmitter and an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) in the transmission channel. The ITS introduces a novel signal modulation architecture for coordinated operation with the base station (BS), while the IRS facilitates efficient signal transmission for the communication users and the sensing target. The main goal is to maximize the beam response gain from the IRS to the sensing target while satisfying the demand of the communication performance for the users. This is realized by collaboratively designing hybrid beamforming strategies at the BS for the simultaneous transmission of communication and sensing signals, along with the ITS and IRS phase shifts. Then, an effective algorithm is proposed that utilizes penalty factors to simplify the optimization problem. Furthermore, an alternating optimization (AO) method is employed to iteratively optimize the relevant variables. Subproblems in this framework are further solved using techniques such as the Lagrange multiplier method, bisection search, the successive convex approximation (SCA), and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme yields a significant enhancement in beam response gain and energy efficiency compared to benchmark schemes.

item.title: Hybrid Classical–Quantum Computing for Joint Latency and Power Optimization of UAV and IRS-Assisted Vehicular Communications
item.description: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted vehicular networks face critical challenges, including dynamic channel conditions, non-line-of-sight (NLoS) signal blockage, and high power consumption, which degrade communication reliability and efficiency in sixth generation (6G) environments. To overcome these limitations, we integrate intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) to dynamically redirect signals, enhancing coverage, and mitigate NLoS losses through adaptive phase-shift control. Furthermore, quantum communication (QC) is leveraged to enable multipartite entanglement across vehicular networks, which uses high-dimensional quantum states transmitted over classical channels to enhance data rates while maintaining fidelity. The objective of this work is to jointly minimize latency and power consumption while maximizing fidelity in IRS-assisted hybrid quantum-classical vehicular networks. Our methodology combines multipartite quantum entanglement with game-theoretic Nash equilibrium to dynamically allocate resources, while IRS optimizes signal reflection paths. The proposed solution is validated through simulations that demonstrate a 40% faster convergence than classical federated learning (FL), a 35% reduction in the use of quantum resources, 20% lower end-to-end latency, and 30% improved UAV power efficiency. These results highlight the superiority of the hybrid QC-IRS approach in achieving reliable and energy-efficient 6G vehicular communications.

item.title: AI-Native Resource Orchestration for Collaborative Sensing, Communication and Computing in UAV-Enabled Space–Air Networks
item.description: Collaborative sensing, communication, and computing (CSCC) empowered Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-enabled air-space networks offer a promising solution for emerging wireless services demanding precise sensing and real-time decision-making in dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose a CSCC framework for space-air networks, in which the UAV both performs data sensing and serves as a relay, offering wireless access between terrestrial sensing devices (TSDs) and the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite edge server. To enhance the adaptability and overall operational efficiency of CSCC systems in dynamic multi-task environments, multiple performance metrics, including sensing satisfaction, service duration, and UAV energy consumption, are jointly considered. Accordingly, by jointly optimizing multi-dimensional heterogeneous resources in each stage of CSCC, we formulate a multi-objective problem with the goal of maximizing the total sensing satisfaction while minimizing the service duration and energy consumption of the UAV. To avoid the curse of dimensionality caused by joint optimization across multiple CSCC stages, we decouple the original optimization problem into two subproblems. Then, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based artificial intelligence (AI)-native algorithmic framework that serves as the intrinsic core engine driving system sensing, decision-making, and execution. Within this framework, the two subproblems can be effectively addressed by using the coordinate descent (CD) based algorithm and the proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based DRL algorithm enhanced with an embedded LSTM module, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms three benchmark methods in terms of convergence, multi-objective performance, and robustness.

item.title: Physical Layer Authentication Enhanced Federated Learning for UAV With Intrinsic Security
item.description: Uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be utilized effectively as airborne base stations, offering wireless communication and federated learning (FL) services for terrestrial edge devices (EDs).FL enables EDs to collaboratively train a global model for specific tasks without sharing their local raw data.However, due to the unreliable wireless links and dynamic topologies, potential malicious nodes may attempt to masquerade as legitimate nodes to pose various potential threats (e.g., inference, poisoning, and backdoor attacks) to undermine the trustworthiness of the intermediate model parameters. Although existing cryptographic authentication protocols focus on the data-level security, security level can be further enhanced at the physical layer level. In this paper, we design FedPLA, a UAV-aided federated learning framework enhanced by physical layer authentication, which utilizes SNR difference for lightweight authentication to ensure FL intrinsic security. Subsequently, we formulate a multi-step decision problem for joint UAV trajectory and resource allocation, aiming to minimize the latency and energy costs while maximizing secure edge device number with intrusion-proof and unjustly accused-proof guaranty. To efficiently deduce strategies while avoiding potential dangerous policies, we develop an LSTM-enhanced safe deep reinforcement learning algorithm (LSTM-SDRL) for real-time strategy making. Furthermore, extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed LSTM-SDRL.

item.title: LAKAS-N: Quantum Attack-Resistant Lattice-Based Authentication and Key Agreement Using NIZK for Single and Cross-Domain VANETs
item.description: Authenticated key exchange and secure handover between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) are essential for the reliability of vehicular networks. However, many existing approaches incur high computational and communication overhead or rely on re-authentication, which limits scalability under high mobility. Moreover, conventional schemes based on classical cryptography cannot withstand quantum adversaries, while lattice-based solutions overlook the need for efficient handover and strong privacy protection. To address these limitations, a lattice-based authentication and key agreement protocol that integrates non-interactive zero-knowledge (NIZK) proofs to enable seamless and post-quantum secure handover in both intra-domain and cross-domain vehicular networks (LAKAS-N) is proposed in this work. The scheme establishes mutual key exchange between vehicles and RSUs, eliminates re-authentication within a single domain, and preserves anonymity when transitioning across domains. Security is rigorously validated through informal and formal analyses, including Scyther-based verification, which confirms resistance against classical and quantum attacks. Lastly, a comprehensive evaluation shows that LAKAS-N achieves stronger security with substantially lower computational, communication, storage, and energy costs compared to state-of-the-art protocols, demonstrating its practicality for real-world vehicular networks.

item.title: Harnessing Cellular Network Data for Accurate Transportation Mode Recognition
item.description: Transportation mode recognition plays a pivotal role in urban planning, environmental research, and smart mobility services. This study introduces a novel data-driven framework leveraging radio access network (RAN) measurements from cellular infrastructure to classify four modes of transportation—car, bus, walk, and train—with high accuracy. Unlike conventional methods that rely on GPS or motion sensors, which are power-intensive and raise privacy concerns, our approach capitalizes on the widespread availability of cellular infrastructure to build the cellular signal features dataset used for classification, ensuring a more energy-efficient, non-intrusive, and scalable solution. Data was collected across two urban cities and a rural university campus, capturing realistic mobility patterns. The proposed system employs gradient-boosted decision trees for classification, achieving a high average $F_{1}$-score of 93.7%. By relying on user-independent inference, the model demonstrates robust performance without requiring personalized data. The results highlight the potential of cellular network data for real-time, privacy-preserving transportation mode detection in support of smart mobility systems.

item.title: Covert Communication Under Stochastic Resonance Eavesdropping: Analysis and Design
item.description: This paper investigates covert communication in the presence of an eavesdropper employing stochastic resonance (SR)–based detection. A unified analytical model is developed to characterize nonlinear noise-matching detectors, with SR serving as a representative example. Closed-form expressions for the achievable covert rate are derived under a KL-divergence-based covertness constraint, revealing that SR-enabled eavesdroppers can significantly enhance detection performance under perfectly matched noise conditions. More importantly, this work establishes a fundamental performance–robustness tradeoff: although stochastic resonance can amplify weak signals, its detection gain is highly sensitive to noise-level mismatch and interference uncertainty. We prove that under random or unknown interference, the worst-case detection performance of SR-based detectors is strictly inferior to that of conventional linear detectors, such as energy detection. This result demonstrates that the detection advantage offered by stochastic resonance is not free and inevitably comes at the cost of robustness. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and show that random, fast-varying interference constitutes a minimax-optimal strategy for covert transmission when the eavesdropper's detection model is unknown. These findings provide new insights into the fundamental limits of covert communication against advanced nonlinear detectors.

item.title: Joint Optimization for Multi-User Transmissive RIS-MIMO Systems
item.description: Transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) represent a transformative architecture for future wireless networks, enabling a paradigm shift from traditional costly base stations to low-cost, energy-efficient transmissive transmitters. This paper explores a downlink multi-user MIMO system where a transmissive RIS, illuminated by a single feed antenna providing an unmodulated carrier, forms the core of the transmitter and embeds user information through programmable time-varying transmissive coefficients. The joint optimization of the RIS coefficient vector, power allocation, and receive beamforming in such a system is critical for performance but poses significant challenges due to the non-convex objective, coupled variables, and constant modulus constraints. To address these challenges, we propose a novel optimization framework. Our approach involves reformulating the sum-rate maximization problem into a tractable equivalent form and developing an efficient alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. This algorithm decomposes the problem into subproblems for the RIS coefficients, receive beamformers, and power allocation, each solved using advanced techniques including convex approximation and difference-of-convex programming. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method converges rapidly and achieves substantial sum-rate gains over conventional schemes, validating the effectiveness of our approach and highlighting the potential of transmissive RIS as a key technology for next-generation wireless systems.

item.title: NOMA-Enabled Joint Sensing and Communication for MISO-Based Non-Terrestrial Networks
item.description: This letter proposes joint sensing and communication (JSAC) for a high-altitude platform station (HAPS) that serves downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) users while simultaneously sensing a ground target. Unlike designs that allocate a dedicated sensing beam, we illuminate the target with the superimposed communication beams and process the echo with a single receive combiner. We formulate a joint transmit–receive design that minimizes the sensing mean-squared error (MSE) under user's minimum rate constraints. The nonconvex problem is addressed by alternating optimization, where the original joint problem is solved in two stages. First, solve the HAPS transmit beamformers problem using semidefinite programming, with the fixed combiner. Then, with the given beamforming, we update the receive combiner in closed form using the linear minimum MSE solution. The proposed NOMA-JSAC solution in HAPS guarantees a monotonic MSE decrease and converges to a stationary solution with low computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate a clear rate–sensing trade-off versus transmit power, validating the practicality and effectiveness of the proposed NOMA-enabled HAPS JSAC design.

item.title: Power-Efficient Beamforming for MI Communication in OAM Systems for SWIPT
item.description: In this paper, we propose a power-efficient Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) framework for Magnetic Induction (MI) systems. By integrating Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) multiplexing with multi-frequency resonance, the proposed transceiver achieves wideband access and full-aperture reuse, allowing all transmit coils to serve every subcarrier simultaneously. We formulate a robust transmit-power minimization problem subject to throughput, harvested-power, and SINR constraints, explicitly accounting for intra-/inter-array coupling and misalignment. A Power-Combination-based Beamforming Scheme (PCBS) is developed to jointly optimize power allocation and splitting ratios. Simulation results demonstrate that PCBS exploits OAM orthogonality to suppress modal leakage, yielding significant transmit-power savings and spectral efficiency gains over single-frequency and non-optimized baselines.

item.title: Cs2PtI6 Perovskite Solar Cells Reimagined: The Synergistic Role of MoS2 Interlayer and Transport Layers Variability in Enhancing Performance
item.description: This study investigates the impact of layer configurations on the performance of Cs2PtI6 perovskite solar cells, focusing on the effects of incorporating a MoS2 interlayer and different electron transport layers (ETLs). Density function theory modeling and optical instigations were employed to validate the forward scattering mechanisms in the MoS2 nanosheets. Six configurations were meticulously analyzed under One Sun optical conditions, revealing significant variations in the power conversion efficiency (PCE). Results indicate that configuration (b), which integrates an MoS2 interlayer with a SnO2 ETL, achieved the highest performance metrics, boasting an experimental ${{{\bm{V}}}_{\mathbf{OC}}}$ of 1.02 V ± 0.1%, ${{{\bm{I}}}_{\mathbf{SC}}}$ of 25.02 mA ± 1.9%, FF of 73.2% ± 2.8%, and a PCE of 18.48% ± 0.9%. This configuration demonstrated an enhanced charge transport mechanism facilitated by the MoS2 interlayer, effectively reducing charge recombination losses and improving energy level alignment between the front electrode and the ETL. In contrast, configurations (e) and (f), which excluded the HTL and interlayer, exhibited significantly lower efficiencies, with PCE values of 10.81% ± 1.8% and 13.97% ± 0.6%, respectively, underscoring the detrimental effects of inadequate charge extraction pathways. Furthermore, the root-mean square error values, concerning numerically simulated data using SCAPS, are notably low for configurations (b) (0.78%) and (d) (0.22%), indicating robust agreement between experimental and simulated outcomes, validating the experimental methodologies employed.

item.title: Experimental Diagnostic and Electrical Characterization of Half-Cut Bifacial PV Module Under Snow Coverage
item.description: Bifacial photovoltaic (BPV) modules are increasingly adopted in northern regions, where snow enhances rear irradiance and energy yield. Despite this potential, snow accumulation and natural melting create complex electrical dynamics that remain underinvestigated at the module level. This work presents a controlled experimental diagnostic of a half-cut BPV module subjected to induced uniform, vertical, and horizontal snow coverage patterns, as well as natural snow-melting process. Monofacial mode was achieved by covering the rear cells with an opaque material and bifacial mode was achieved by removing the cover. Experimental results show that a uniform 3 cm snow layer causes an 84% power loss in monofacial mode compared to clear-sky conditions. Bifacial operation reduces the loss to 72%, representing an 83% power improvement over monofacial mode under snow. Under patterned snow bands covering $< 50\%$ of the module area, vertical bands induce a 52% power loss, double the 26% loss under horizontal patterns. This highlights the strategic advantage of half-cut architecture during natural bottom-up snow accumulation. Finally, tracking of natural melting reveals three regimes: static thinning, cracking/sliding, and recovery. Throughout these phases, $V_{\text{mpp}}$ and fill factor (FF) exhibit pronounced volatility in contrast to a remarkable relative stability of $V_{\text{oc}}$. Notably, the FF is found to increase under specific partial snow-cover geometries, reaching a peak of 85%, and decrease under clear-sky levels. These results demonstrate that static derating factors fail to capture the highly dynamic physics of snow-affected BPV modules. These diagnostic signatures provide the foundational phenomenology to evaluate and improve the accuracy of standard electrical models in replicating these complex, shape-dependent operating states.

item.title: Impact of Light-Soaking Preconditioning for Measurements of Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
item.description: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) have attracted significant attention in the photovoltaic field because of their excellent power conversion efficiency. However, the inherent instability of PSTSCs has led to a mismatch between existing testing standards and accurate performance evaluation. Although preconditioning brings the cells close to steady-state prior to measurements, specific preconditioning methods remain undefined. In this study, we systematically investigated the effects of light-soaking preconditioning (LSPC) of PSTSCs under open-circuit, short-circuit, and maximum power point (MPP) conditions on their electrical performance parameters. The results showed that LSPC under open-circuit conditions caused an initial improvement in efficiency, followed by continuous degradation, and short-term stabilization did not guarantee sustained performance stability. Preconditioning under short-circuit conditions resulted in a significant decline in cell performance, suggesting that this condition was unsuitable for preconditioning. In contrast, preconditioning under MPP conditions enabled both unencapsulated and encapsulated cells to achieve stability, with efficiency fluctuations less than 2%. Moreover, the efficiency values obtained from reverse I–V scans following MPP preconditioning were consistent with those monitored by maximum power point tracking (MPPT). On the basis of these findings, an efficient and reliable measurement protocol for PSTSCs was proposed: LSPC under MPP conditions for at least 10 min, followed by I–V scanning. This protocol allowed quick and accurate determination of the performance parameters of PSTSCs, providing guidance for standardized characterization of PSTSCs.

item.title: Comparison of Indoor Characterization and Outdoor Energy Yield Measurements of Shade-Resistant and Standard PV Modules Under Partial Shading Conditions
item.description: The current energy crisis in Europe demands more renewable energy installation. Looking into the photovoltaic (PV) installations in Germany and The Netherlands, rooftop installations dominate about the share of 45% and 80% of the installations in these countries, respectively. However, rooftops have elements, such as chimneys and antennas, which can cast shadows leading to a drastic energy loss. Typical PV modules have three bypass diodes per module protecting the strings. In extreme cases, only 5% shading of the module area can lead to a total shutdown of the PV module by triggering the bypass diodes. Therefore, AESOLAR has developed a shade-resistant and hot-spot-free PV module to address this challenge and maximize the energy yield in a limited area. The PV module has integrated bypass diodes for each solar cell, showing up to 45% more energy yield than a similar standard module under partial shading conditions. In this work, we analyze and compare the indoor characterization and the outdoor energy yield of the shade-resistant and standard PV modules of AESOLAR that are made from a similar bill of materials under partial shading conditions. The results show a significant advantage in yield production compared to the standard module.

item.title: Qualification of Photovoltaic Micromodules for Energy Harvesting With Applications in IoT Systems: PCA and Fuzzy Statistical Approach
item.description: This article investigates the qualification of photovoltaic micromodules intended for energy harvesting in Internet-of-Things systems, with emphasis on the degradation mechanisms induced by accelerated environmental aging typical of tropical conditions. This study employs multiple complementary characterization techniques—including pulsed current–voltage measurements, electroluminescence imaging, and impedance spectroscopy—combined with multidomain statistical analysis to support decision-making regarding acceptance criteria and failure mode clustering. The work addresses a regulatory gap affecting photovoltaic devices below 5 Wp, a class of modules whose deployment is rapidly expanding in remote, autonomous, and low-power Internet of Things applications, yet remains largely unsupported by certification standards. Together, these procedures establish a unified methodology that integrates electrical, structural, and statistical perspectives, forming a robust analytical foundation for qualification and degradation assessment, acceptance criteria definition, and comparative analysis of PV micromodules.

item.title: Photovoltaic and Battery System Sizing Optimization for Electric Car-Sharing: An Energy and Economic Assessment
item.description: The growing adoption of electric vehicle (EV) car-sharing, while contributing to reduced traffic congestion and urban pollution, still presents concerns related to energy supply. Since most grid electricity is still fossil-based, global environmental benefits remain limited. Integrating photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) into EV charging hubs (CH) offers a promising solution. However, optimal system sizing is critical to balance energy benefits and cost-effectiveness. This study proposes a multiobjective optimization method to determine the optimal size of PV-BESS systems integrated with an EV CH, maximizing energy self-sufficiency while minimizing annual total cost. To enhance battery lifetime estimation, a semiempirical battery degradation model is developed. The method is evaluated using the power demand profile of a real-world CH in Bologna. A multicountry analysis across six European nations, which includes Spain, Denmark, Italy, Germany, France, and The Netherlands, assesses how varying solar radiation and electricity costs affect system performance. Results show that self-sufficiency ranges from 51% in Denmark to 72% in Italy and Spain. The optimally sized PV-BESS configuration is economically advantageous for all countries except Denmark, and, in general, pursuing higher self-sufficiency levels leads to exponentially increasing costs, revealing diminishing economic returns.

item.title: Effect of Light Source Intensity Distribution on the Laser Power Transmission System Efficiency
item.description: Laser power transmission (LPT) has emerged as a promising technology for long-distance wireless energy transfer, whose system efficiency strongly depends on the output characteristics of the light source. This study systematically investigates the effect of light source intensity distribution on LPT system efficiency by comparing Gaussian and flat-top beams. Numerical models were established to analyze the evolution of atmospheric transmittance and spot uniformity under various atmospheric conditions over transmission distances ranging from 40 to 200 m. LPT experiments were conducted under realistic atmospheric conditions to confirm the trends predicted by the simulations. Results demonstrate that flat-top beams exhibit consistently higher atmospheric transmittance and superior spot uniformity compared with Gaussian beams. As the transmission distance increased from 40 to 200 m, the atmospheric transmittance decreased from 93.11% to 82.41% for Gaussian beams and from 96.11% to 86.19% for flat-top beams. Simultaneously, the spot uniformity declined from 52.18% to 30.80% for Gaussian beams and from 65.81% to 47.35% for flat-top beams. Finally, the LPT system efficiency achieved with flat-top beams is on average 3.42% higher than that with Gaussian beams. These findings provide critical insights into the design of light sources for practical LPT system, contributing to enhanced robustness and efficiency.

item.title: Shading Effects of Thin-Film Photovoltaic Modules
item.description: Thin-film photovoltaic modules are often assumed to exhibit a linear reduction in output power when subjected to partial shading. However, this practice lacks a firm foundation in the literature. We experimentally demonstrate the linear response to partial shading using indoor flash testing of a commercial First Solar Series 6 thin-film module. We also demonstrate that a simple linear irradiance adjustment results in accurate energy yield simulations using data from a utility-scale thin-film photovoltaic system. Finally, to facilitate future work in this area, we document our simple and efficient method of measuring the impact of partial shading in a flash tester using a semitransparent material mimicking shading conditions in the field.

item.title: Chiplet-Based Techniques for Scalable and Memory-Aware Multiscalar Multiplication on Hardware Platforms
item.description: This article presents a high-performance architecture for accelerating multiscalar multiplication (MSM) on ASIC platforms, targeting cryptographic applications with high throughput and scalability demands. Current MSM accelerators on FPGA and ASIC platforms typically focus on designing efficient processing elements (PEs) to perform resource-intensive elliptic curve point operations, which require a high number of 384-bit modular multipliers. Our approach diverges from existing works by adopting a chiplet-based design, which optimally balances area, power consumption, and computational throughput. By analyzing memory requirements across window sizes, we determine an optimal mixed configuration of 12- and 13-bit windows, which allows efficient integration of multiple PEs per chiplet. Considering the single-PE case, our design achieves a 1.37x speedup and a 1.3x area reduction over prior works. Moreover, our multi-PE chiplet design outperforms monolithic designs by 2.2x in area–time product while allowing lower production costs and higher yield.

item.title: Analog Power Consumption Analysis of TI-ADC Architectures for Wireless Communication
item.description: A modeling framework for power efficiency in high-speed time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TI-ADCs) is proposed. Estimating the power contributions of the sub-ADCs, interleaving circuits, and clock distribution enables an informed architectural tradeoff to balance performance goals. An signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) sensitivity analysis to interleaving mismatches, offering insights for the calibration algorithm design, complements it for robust architecture selection. The methodology’s applicability and limitations are illustrated through two case studies.

item.title: A CDAC-Interleaved OTA-Free Fourth-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC With Twofold Passive Gain
item.description: To address the tradeoffs among noise-shaping (NS) performance, energy efficiency, and area overhead in conventional time-interleaved (TI) NS successive-approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), this article proposes an OTA-free TI NS-SAR ADC. The architecture interleaves only the capacitive digital-to-analog converters (CDACs) across channels, while the comparators, integrator, and digital logic are shared. Furthermore, this work realizes a 4th-order integrator that enables aggressive noise shaping ability. Additionally, the design incorporates a robust $2\times $ passive gain technique. It reduces the required gains of the fine five-input-pair comparator by half, thus lowering its power consumption. Fabricated in 28 nm CMOS process, the prototype occupies 0.038 mm2. Measurement results show that, operating at 300 MS/s under a 1 V supply, the ADC consumes 4.77 mW. It achieves 77.6 dB SNDR and 88.6 dB SFDR over a 15 MHz bandwidth, achieving a Schreier FoM (FoMS) of 172.6 dB.

item.title: A 10-Gb/s NRZ/PAM-4 Compatible Transceiver Using 8b/10b Recovery for Automotive Applications
item.description: This article proposes a transceiver that converts 10-Gb/s 8b/10b-encoded non-return-to-zero (NRZ) data into pulse-amplitude modulation-4 (PAM-4) data for long-channel communication. To ensure compatibility with conventional NRZ systems, the proposed transmitter (TX) integrates a 10-Gb/s NRZ analog front-end (AFE) with clock-and-data recovery (CDR), an 8b/10b recovery circuit, and a PAM-4 TX.
