Correspondingly, the receiver (RX) chip consists of a PAM-4 RX with a 5-Gbaud CDR and a 10-Gb/s NRZ output driver. The proposed 8b/10b recovery circuit addresses DC balance issues inherent in NRZ-to-PAM-4 conversion, thereby enhancing signal integrity (SI) and simplifying the CDR design in the PAM-4 RX. Specifically, the recovery circuit restores the disparity characteristics to a range of −2 to +2 and reduces the standard deviation of the data run length from 2.08 to 1.70. Furthermore, the threshold calibration for the PAM-4 RX increases the time and voltage margins of the received data. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process with a 1.2-V supply, the transceiver converts 10-Gb/s NRZ data into 5.0-Gbaud PAM-4 data and vice versa. Measurement results demonstrate that the proposed 8b/10b recovery circuit improves the root mean square (rms) time jitter of the recovered clock by 12% while successfully restoring the 8b/10b training pattern. The TX and RX chips consume 68 and 67 mW, respectively, with active areas of 0.30 and 0.34 mm2.

item.title: A Closed-Loop System for Extracting Programming Parameters in Breakdown-Based OTP Memory
item.description: Breakdown-based one-time-programmable (OTP) concepts such as gate-oxide antifuses are attractive for compact, logic-compatible storage of immutable security credentials and calibration data. However, dielectric breakdown exhibits strong sensitivity to oxide thickness, defect statistics, and stress history, making fixed worst case programming recipes inefficient and potentially overstress-prone. This article presents an autonomous programming-parameter extraction system that identifies a die-specific programming-voltage and pulsewidth pair using a closed-loop current-trip condition and a self-regulating high-voltage (HV) charge-pump generator. The proposed system performs an ordered 2-D search over quantized voltage and time candidates, freezes the programming word at the first verified conduction event. Fabricated in 180 nm CMOS, the prototype demonstrates quantized programming-voltage generation from 5.2 to 12.5 V, programmable stress windows of 14.2, 28.2, and 56.7 ms, and $\mathrm {363~\mu W}$ full-cycle search power. Measurements using actual antifuse test structures show a breakdown event at 8.97 V after 13.8 ms within the second 14.2 ms candidate window. With a 1 mA current clamp, numerical integration over the measured $\mathrm {400~\mu s}$ postbreakdown connected interval gives a post-trip stress energy of $\mathrm {0.985~\mu J}$ .

item.title: Cross-Domain Hardware Trojans at the ADC Boundary in Mixed-Signal ICs
item.description: Mixed-signal system-on-chips (SoCs) rely on the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) to isolate analog uncertainty from digital computation, with small perturbations expected to appear as uncorrelated stochastic variations in the least significant bits (LSBs). This work demonstrates that this assumption can be violated. We introduce a cross-domain hardware Trojan (HT) that originates in the analog power supply network and propagates through the ADC boundary, where structured perturbations within the effective noise envelope induce deterministic patterns in the digital domain. As a result, the proposed HT enables controlled cross-domain influence without modifying digital logic inputs or producing observable anomalies under standard validation and test methodologies. We show that this class of HT evades conventional analog and digital detection approaches, including power-supply testing and functional verification, which rely on assumptions of observable perturbations or digital-domain activation. The attack is validated through mixed-signal case studies demonstrating logic manipulation and privilege escalation, and is experimentally verified using a custom-fabricated analog, mixed-signal (AMS) chip and field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based digital backend, achieving low hardware overhead while maintaining indistinguishability from nominal signal behavior.

item.title: A CLS-Based Driven Classified Truncation Approximate Booth Multiplier for High-Fidelity Image Processing
item.description: To address the energy-efficiency constraints of arithmetic units in high-fidelity image processing applications, a classified truncation compensation approximate Booth multiplier driven by constrained level selection (CLS) is proposed in this article. The proposed approach models low-weight partial-product contributions and realizes fixed-boundary truncation with input-dependent classified compensation to reduce hardware overhead while controlling truncation-induced bias. Based on the proposed method, three 8-bit approximate multipliers are implemented by combining approximate Booth encoders, approximate 4–2 compressors, and truncation-compensation schemes. Synthesis results in TSMC 90 nm CMOS technology show that, compared with the exact multiplier, the lowest-cost design reduces area, power consumption, and power delay product (PDP) by 37.9%, 32.9%, and 83.4%, respectively, while maintaining low NMED and MRED. Furthermore, Gaussian filtering, image sharpening, and Sobel edge detection experiments demonstrate that the proposed accuracy-oriented design maintains high perceptual image quality across different convolution-based image processing tasks.

item.title: A Custom Hardware Accelerator for Softmax Function With Parallel Online Normalization
item.description: Softmax computation in transformer-based LLM/SLM models commonly relies on online normalization to ensure numerical stability while reducing memory access cycles. However, conventional online formulations introduce loop-carried dependencies that result in serialization, restricting scalable spatial parallelism, and efficient wide-datapath realization in hardware implementations. This article presents a custom Softmax hardware accelerator (CSHA) based on an algorithm–architecture codesigned parallel online normalization framework. The proposed algorithm reformulates sequential online normalization into a parallel streaming-compatible structure while preserving numerical stability and memory efficiency, thereby enabling scalable datapath parallelism. All core computational units—maximum detection, exponential approximation, reduction trees, multiplication, and logarithmic computation—are circuit-optimized and synthesized in a 90 nm CMOS process to evaluate area, power, and delay tradeoffs. The CSHA employs a fully pipelined fixed-point architecture designed for accuracy-aware hardware efficiency. System-level validation is performed by replacing the floating-point Softmax in a pretrained BERT model with the proposed implementation, demonstrating less than 1% accuracy degradation across GLUE tasks and the SQuAD dataset. Field programmable gate array (FPGA) deployment on a Zynq-7000 SoC further verifies functional correctness and dynamic sequence-length configurability, eliminating redundant padded Softmax computation. By integrating algorithm reformulation with circuit-level optimization, the proposed CSHA provides an efficient and scalable oSftmax solution suitable for low-power, high-throughput inference systems.

item.title: TetraPIXA: A High-Performance and Resource-Efficient Accelerator for Pillar and Voxel Feature Networks in 3-D Point Cloud Object Detection
item.description: Point cloud data (PCD) acquired using 3-D sensing technologies offer unique advantages over 2-D camera images in applications such as robotics and autonomous driving. In particular, voxel- and pillar-based point cloud neural networks (PNNs) have demonstrated strong performance in large-scale outdoor 3-D object detection scenarios. However, due to the irregular, sparse, and unordered nature of PCD, prior approaches, including GPU-based solutions, struggle to process such data efficiently and typically require substantial hardware resources. To address these challenges, this article proposes TetraPIXA, a high-performance and resource-efficient accelerator that employs a unified architecture supporting both voxel feature network (VFN) and pillar feature network (PFN), which serve as the critical preprocessing stages where these challenges primarily arise. By exploiting spatial locality, TetraPIXA enables independent operation of multiple cores, thereby achieving effective data-level parallelism. In addition, temporal locality is leveraged to significantly reduce the latency of time-consuming and exhaustive pillar-voxel (PV) operations without introducing additional hardware overhead. For feature encoding (FE), which involves compute-intensive multiply–accumulate (MAC) operations, TetraPIXA incorporates a resource-aware parallel and pipelined (RAPP) architecture in conjunction with spatial locality to achieve resource-efficient acceleration. TetraPIXA was implemented and evaluated on an FPGA platform and achieves up to $39.9\times $ speedup over prior works with a power consumption of only 1.2 W, while maintaining the detection accuracy of the full-precision baseline.

item.title: ME-MoD: Algorithm-Hardware-Dataflow Co-Design for Memory Efficient Mixture-of-Depth-Based Vision Transformer Accelerator
item.description: Transformers outperform traditional neural networks but face high computational and memory costs, limiting edge device deployment. Although many hardware accelerators aim to address this, the original Transformer structure still restricts the optimization effect. A recent breakthrough, mixture-of-depths (MoDs), employs conditional computation and effectively reduces the computational complexity of large language models, providing a valuable opportunity for designing an efficient hardware accelerator. However, when applied to vision transformers, MoD suffers from accuracy degradation and excessive external memory access (EMA). Therefore, this article presents ME-MoD, the first memory-efficient MoD-based vision transformer inference accelerator, leveraging the idea of reordering and algorithm-hardware-dataflow codesign. Algorithmically, distribution adjustment forward (DAF) and routing decision forward (RDF) techniques restore accuracy and alleviate memory access costs through token reordering. Architecturally, a LayerNorm-Routing (L-R) fusion module and a token reordering and sequential recording module enhance computational efficiency while minimizing memory overhead. In addition, a token-stationary layer fusion dataflow and an on-chip dynamic memory module are designed, which further optimizes the EMA caused by the intermediate results of interlayer computation of valid tokens routed by MoD. With negligible accuracy loss, our ME-MoD accelerator achieves $1.62\times $ inference speed up, eliminates 46.5% of the external memory bandwidth requirement and 45.2% of energy consumption compared with standard MoD. It achieves 23.6 TOPS/W energy efficiency, which is $4.02\times $ improvements compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) designs.

item.title: Workload-Aware Compressor Tree Design Automation With Statistical Calibration for Efficient AI Accelerators
item.description: A compressor tree is an essential building block of multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) units, hierarchically reducing multiple partial sums without immediate carry propagation. This article introduces a workload-aware compressor tree synthesis framework that aligns model-level noise tolerance with hardware-level arithmetic design to enable statistically guided MAC in artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators. Unlike conventional compressor trees that rely on uniform approximation policies, the proposed approach derives an allowable error budget by analyzing noise–accuracy behavior and profiling workload-specific bit-pattern distributions, revealing that most significant bit (MSB) regions are biased toward high-Hamming-weight values, such as all-ones and near-all-ones cases. Guided by these statistics, the framework automatically selects among exact and approximate compressors from a characterization library, and incorporates a pattern-accurate 6:3 compressor designed to minimize MSB-sensitive error while preserving hardware efficiency. This unified flow generates compressor trees that remain compliant with model-derived accuracy constraints while significantly reducing cost. Fabricated in a commercial 28 nm process, the resulting designs improve delay and power by up to 15%–25% across diverse convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer models, achieving 14–27 TOPS/W while maintaining only 0.07% average inference accuracy degradation. These results highlight that workload-calibrated accumulation is a critical optimization axis for modern AI accelerators and demonstrate the value of statistically specialized compressor structures for domain-specific edge inference accelerator deployments.

item.title: A 22-nm End-to-End Edge--AI Processor With Booth-Value-Confined Acceleration and Hardware-Aware Layer-Wise Model Deployment
item.description: Edge devices capable of running artificial intelligence (AI) applications have seen a surge in demand for energy-efficient and high-throughput computation. In this study, a 22-nm edge–AI processor, incorporating an accelerator with error-free Booth-value-confined (BVC) multiprecision (MP) multiplier and near-memory computing (NMC), is introduced to accelerate neural networks (NNs). It has the following three major features. First, a BVC MP multiplier based on radix-8 Booth (R8B) is introduced to reduce computation complexity by prohibiting the “±3” cases and support error-free training on GPU without accuracy loss originating from the mismatch between training and deployment. A PE is built based on this multiplier for parallel computation with 82% power reduction and 70% area reduction. Second, the proposed NMC-friendly data flow supports efficient data reuse and hence reduces off-chip memory traffic. The data flow supports data reuse of up to 16 times, matching the number of PEs and enabling regular read and write patterns. Third, a hardware-aware layer-wise model deployment approach is proposed with a memory space contiguity-aware (MSCA) model reshape strategy, and a hardware-aware NN splitting and scheduling algorithm. The proposed MSCA strategy maximizes burst access, and the proposed algorithm achieves efficient computation with high data reuse and low memory access. This deployment approach can achieve a reduction in memory access latency of 16.6%–32.0%. Measurements on a 22-nm test chip demonstrate a peak power efficiency of 33.98 TOPS/W under synthetic full-PE-utilization conditions, while achieving 12.92–29.11 TOPS/W for end-to-end NN inference on DarkNet19, VGG16, ViT-Tiny, and ResNet34.

item.title: 7T SRAM Macro Supporting 2W/2R Adjacent Dual-Row Access for Enhanced Memory Bandwidth and Energy Efficiency
item.description: This article proposes a 7T static random access memory (SRAM) macro using an adjacent dual-row simultaneous access (DRSA) scheme based on an independent single-ended bitline control (ISBC) technique. Using this technique, the SRAM enables simultaneous dual-write (2W) or dual-read (2R) operations on two adjacent rows within a single cycle, thereby achieving a $2\times $ bandwidth improvement over conventional single-row access (SRA) SRAMs. Accordingly, the proposed DRSA scheme significantly improves energy efficiency and latency by reducing the number of access cycles required for a given workload. Designed in a 28-nm CMOS process, the 4-Kb 7T SRAM macro demonstrates a total active energy of 0.163 pJ/access/bit in DRSA mode, which is $0.75\times $ that of a conventional SRA SRAM.

item.title: HierCIM: A 16-Kb SRAM-Based Digital CIM Macro With Hierarchical Adder-Tree Accumulation for Edge CNN Inference
item.description: The growing demand for efficient deep-learning inference on edge platforms requires hardware that is both energy-efficient and practically implementable. This work presents a 16-Kb all-digital static random-access memory (SRAM)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) macro for low-bit CNN inference, featuring a hierarchical adder-tree-based accumulation architecture. The design integrates a nor-enabled SRAM compute cell, column-wise rearrangement network, sparsity-aware compression, and multistage hierarchical accumulation within a 64-bank $64 \,\, \times \,\, 4$ architecture, enabling scalable bit-serial processing and utilization-aware mapping. Implemented in 65-nm CMOS, the macro achieves 8.19 TOPS effective throughput at 1.0 V and a peak energy efficiency of 586 TOPS/W at 0.9 V under practical operating conditions. Hardware-compatible CNN mapping is demonstrated using LeNet-5, VGG-8, and ResNet-8. The design achieves 98.1% and 72.3% accuracy on MNIST and CIFAR-10, respectively, with 1-bit activations and 4-bit weights, while 4-bit configurations on deeper networks show only 3%–4% degradation from FP32 baselines. CNN inference is evaluated using a hardware-compatible post-training quantization (PTQ) flow without retraining. These results demonstrate that the proposed SRAM-CIM architecture provides an efficient and scalable accumulation solution with a practical tradeoff among throughput, energy efficiency, and implementability for edge-oriented deep neural network (DNN) inference.

item.title: EVA: Efficient Token Compression Co-Optimization With Heterogeneous CIM Architecture for Video LLM Acceleration
item.description: Video large language models (VLLMs) enable powerful multimodal reasoning but face severe efficiency challenges on edge devices due to the massive computational and memory demands caused by lengthy video-token sequences. Existing methods struggle to efficiently compress spatiotemporally redundant tokens while minimizing DRAM access overhead during inference. In this work, we propose EVA, a co-designed algorithm–hardware framework for accelerating VLLMs. At the algorithm level, we introduce an efficient training-free token compression (ETC) method that combines greedy temporal segmentation (GTS) to adaptively partition frames by content similarity, with diversity spatiotemporal compression (DSC) to retain semantically rich tokens from both static and dynamic regions. The method is plug-and-play, requires no retraining, and employs sign similarity to enable hardware-friendly computing at scale. At the hardware level, we design a heterogeneous accelerator integrating a lightweight token compression engine (TCE), a computing-in-memory (CIM) engine for in situ execution of linear layers, and a reconfigurable digital attention engine with hardware-specialized attention computation and an interleaved pipeline dataflow. Across multiple models and video benchmarks, EVA preserves accuracy under aggressive token reduction and delivers substantial efficiency gains. Notably, on LLaVA-OneVision-7B, EVA compresses 90% of video tokens while maintaining 97.8% of the original accuracy. EVA achieves up to $10.3\times $ speedup and $47.4\times $ energy reduction compared to GPU, and achieves up to $3.8\times $ speedup over prior specialized accelerators, demonstrating a practical path toward scalable VLLM inference on resource-constrained devices.

item.title: GFRA: A High-Utilization Grain-Fused Reconfigurable Architecture for Coarse-Grained and Fine-Grained Applications
item.description: The evolving computational tasks impose higher demands on hardware resource utilization. Coarse-grained reconfigurable architectures (CGRAs), owing to their high flexibility and energy efficiency, exhibit significant potential in addressing these demands. However, when CGRAs handle hybrid coarse-grained (CG) and fine-grained (FG) operations—such as CG arithmetic operations like multiply-accumulate and FG operations like and/or—the processing elements (PEs) cannot be fully utilized for CG computation because some PEs are allocated to FG tasks. This results in low PE resource utilization and further limits the parallel acceleration capability of CGRAs. To address this, we propose a high-utilization grain-fused reconfigurable architecture (GFRA) that integrates Boolean processor (BP) technology. The GFRA architecture, incorporating Boolean processor technology, is implemented to optimize CG and FG computations, thereby improving CG resource utilization and parallel acceleration capability. The core idea of GFRA is that CGRA offloads FG computations to Boolean processors to achieve parallel acceleration. Specifically, dedicated computing units for CG and FG operations, optimized interconnection paths, and a hierarchical management approach for information flow are proposed, enhancing the architecture’s efficiency in handling control flow, configuration flow, and data flow for hybrid-grained tasks. Compared with representative CGRAs, GFRA achieves an average CG resource utilization of 90.4%, an average normalized speedup improvement of 48.5%, and an average normalized execution time reduction of 45.7%, and demonstrates the best performance in cryptographic tasks.

item.title: Routing-Aware In Situ Diagnosis of PDN- and Configuration-Induced Delay Signatures in SRAM-Based FPGAs
item.description: Timing degradation in static random-access memory (SRAM)-based field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) can arise from multiple physical mechanisms, including power-distribution-network (PDN) stress and configuration-induced routing perturbations. Although both appear as the delay increases, their spatial and statistical signatures differ. This article presents a routing-aware in situ diagnosis framework that observes timing behavior at selected switch-matrix-accessible routing nodes during operation. The method combines nonintrusive delay taps (DTs), phase-swept sampling, and centralized statistical analysis to extract BER-versus-phase timing signatures from tapped routing signals. Experimental results on an Xilinx/AMD XCZU7EV FPGA show that PDN-induced effects produce broadly correlated delay shifts with limited variance growth, whereas configuration-induced routing perturbations produce localized, topology-dependent delay increases and stronger dispersion. Spatial correlation analysis further separates these mechanisms through their distinct correlation decay patterns. The proposed framework is intended for comparative diagnosis and spatial characterization of routing-observable timing degradation rather than complete path coverage or immediate timing-failure protection. The implementation uses lightweight instrumentation and scales linearly with the number of monitored routing locations, making it suitable for targeted in-fabric timing diagnosis in deployed FPGA systems.

item.title: Hardware--Algorithm Co-Design for Efficient Bit-Serial Acceleration of Lightweight CNNs With Standard and Depthwise Convolutions on FPGA
item.description: Bit-serial computation (BSC) is attractive for field-programmable gated array (FPGA)-based convolutional neural network (CNN) acceleration because it naturally supports mixed-precision quantization and bit-level sparse computation. However, MobileNetV2-like lightweight CNNs contain standard convolution (SC) and depthwise separable convolution (DSC) layers, which impose different bottlenecks on conventional BSC. SC layers provide sufficient input-channel parallelism but suffer from redundant weight-bit computation, whereas DSC layers have only one input channel and cause severe utilization mismatch with fixed input-channel-parallel bit-serial MAC units. To address these issues, this paper proposes an operator-aware hardware–algorithm co-design framework. For SC layers, mixed-precision quantization (MPQ) and column-based bit-level sparsity (CBBLS) are jointly adopted to reduce effective weight-bit computation. For DSC layers, a dataflow-reconfigurable bit-serial MAC (DR-BSMAC) is proposed to improve hardware utilization. Implemented on an Xilinx VCU118 FPGA at 300 MHz, the proposed accelerator achieves 806.5 GOPS on MobileNetV2 with only 1.48% top-1 accuracy loss on ImageNet, providing $2.39\times $ overall throughput improvement over the 8-bit baseline. The same framework also achieves 581.9 GOPS and $2.27\times $ speedup on EfficientNet-B0. Compared with state-of-the-art accelerators, our design improves equivalent LUT efficiency and energy efficiency by up to $7.03\times $ and $4.74\times $ on MobileNetV2 and by up to $16.50\times $ and $4.49\times $ on EfficientNet-B0, respectively. The DR-BSMAC RTL is publicly available at https://github.com/haden-01/DR-BSMAC.git

item.title: Low-Power FPGA Implementation of Twin Support Vector Machine-Based Epileptic Seizure Detection Algorithm
item.description: In neurological research, detecting epileptic seizures is the most crucial task using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for clinical applications. Implementing a conventional support vector machine (SVM) for seizure detection is computationally intensive for real-time applications. The twin SVM (TSVM), a variant of SVM, along with the sequential minimal optimization (SMO) algorithm, is appropriate for hardware acceleration as it provides reduced computational complexity with better classification performance. In order to detect seizures in real-time using EEG signals, this article presents the field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based implementation of the TSVM framework accelerated using the SMO algorithm for efficient real-time seizure detection on an Xilinx Virtex 7 FPGA board. The proposed framework follows a software–hardware (S/H) co-design methodology, in which EEG preprocessing, normalization, feature extraction, and feature selection are implemented in MATLAB, whereas the SMO optimization engine and TSVM classifier are implemented on FPGA hardware, thereby achieving better computation with minimal power consumption through efficient arithmetic operations and parallel processing. The proposed design is validated on benchmark EEG datasets from the CHB-MIT dataset, achieving high classification accuracy and low latency when implemented with a linear kernel TSVM. Besides that, it uses $1.6\times $ less power compared to the earlier performed implementation in prior work using SVM. A more accurate diagnosis through TSVM may lead to better treatment and patient care. The development of TSVM and SMO algorithms is expected to improve seizure detection and treatment. It will, in turn, allow for more efficient and effective medical solutions.

item.title: New Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in Resource-Constrained Montgomery Ladder Scalar Multiplication Based on Projective Coordinates
item.description: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) primitives over prime fields are integral to many security protocols due to their compact key sizes and strong security. Scalar multiplication is a complex operation at the core of ECC algorithms. Scalar multiplication is often implemented following the Montgomery ladder to mitigate side-channel power analysis risks due to its uniform execution pattern. This work introduces new side-channel vulnerabilities on the ladder when facing resource-constrained hardware requirements for implementing potential projective coordinate formulations. The new vulnerability is exploited through mounting a full-stack horizontal power analysis (HPA) attack using as few as a single power trace in some cases.

item.title: A Tiny Neuromorphic Processor Enabling On-Chip Spike-Based Learning for Edge Intelligent System
item.description: Neuromorphic processors deploying spiking neural networks (SNNs) hold great potential for edge intelligence applications. However, achieving high accuracy, high throughput, and highly energy-efficient on-chip learning under limited energy and resource budgets remains a critical challenge. To address this, we propose a tiny neuromorphic architecture to support a fully spike-based backpropagation learning algorithm tailored for a lightweight two-layer SNN aiming at edge scenarios. To enhance processing efficiency, this architecture tightly couples control and data flows, and features fully spike-based inference and learning. Furthermore, we propose a structured weight mapping scheme that satisfies different parallel memory access patterns during forward and backward passes, and introduce a group-based event-driven paradigm to exploit spike sparsity. A prototype was implemented on a very-low-cost Xilinx Zynq-7010 FPGA device. It achieved high on-chip learning accuracies comparable to state-of-the-art works across multiple benchmark datasets, while delivering a throughput of 2269/9082 frames/s and an energy efficiency of 56/ $14~\mu $ J/image for learning/inferring MNIST images, which outperforms existing approaches and shows its potential for wide deployments in extreme edge intelligence scenarios.

item.title: A 2-kHz BW 89.2-dB SNDR 100-dB SFDR Σ–Δ DAC for Precision Instruments
item.description: This brief presents a $\Sigma $ – $\Delta $ digital-to-analog converter (DAC) for precision instruments. To enhance the power efficiency, a direct-charge-transfer (DCT) DAC is proposed. In addition, an analog smoothing filter is integrated to suppress the high-frequency noise, enhancing the quality of the output signal. Compared with the traditional filter off-chip strategy, on-chip active filters enable a better suppression of out-of-band noise and harmonics. This work adopts a co-design approach in which the on-chip active filter and the data-weighted averaging (DWA)-DCT path are jointly optimized to suppress switching glitches and out-of-band noise, thereby enabling high-precision performance. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the proposed $\Sigma $ – $\Delta $ DAC occupies an area of 0.43 mm2 and consumes 3.68 mW from a 3.3-V supply. On condition that the sampling frequency (f ${}_{\mathrm {s}}$ ) is set to be 256 kS/s, the DAC achieves a maximum signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 89.2 dB and a spurious-free-dynamic-range (SFDR) of 100 dB over 2-kHz bandwidth. The maximum differential nonlinearity error (DNL) is 0.36 LSB, indicating no missing code for static applications.

item.title: Metastability-Based Time-Gain-Enhanced Voltage-to-Time Converter With Time-Offset Calibration for Time-Domain Applications
item.description: Voltage-to-time converters (VTCs) utilizing metastability are widely used in high-speed applications, where the VTC gain is critical because it affects input sensitivity and the sampling margin. However, existing methods for high VTC gain often introduce additional challenges. To address this issue, this brief introduces a metastability-based double-tail VTC incorporating a cross-coupled nMOS pair in the dynamic preamplifier. This structure increases the clock (CLK)-to-Q delay at small input voltages while minimizing the delay increase at large inputs, thereby enhancing the VTC gain. In addition, a binary-weighted $g_{m}$ control time-offset calibration circuit compensates for delay variations caused by device mismatch and process, voltage, and temperature variations, and a CLK-separated comparator structure eliminates short-circuit current paths for power saving. Postlayout simulations in 65-nm CMOS technology at a 0.8-V VDD show that the VTC gain increased from 0.24 to 0.449 ps/mV.

item.title: An Energy-Efficient GPS Acquisition Macro Using Accurate Approximate SRAM-PIM for Low-Power GNSS Applications
item.description: The signal acquisition, one of the most computation-intensive stages in global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receivers, dominates both power consumption and area overhead. To reduce global positioning system (GPS) acquisition latency and improve receiver energy efficiency, this brief proposes an energy-efficient GPS acquisition macro based on accurate/approximate static random-access memory (SRAM) processing-in-memory (PIM). The proposed design performs parallel code-phase and Doppler-frequency searches through PIM-based convolution and discrete Fourier transform (DFT) operations, eliminating the need for a real-time coarse acquisition (C/A)-code generator, thereby reducing data movement and acquisition power. An accurate/approximate dual-mode computing strategy is introduced to enable a flexible tradeoff between acquisition probability and energy efficiency under different signal environments. Moreover, a flexible GPS acquisition workflow supporting both convolution and convolution-DFT algorithms is developed to improve the generality of the architecture, thereby enhancing architectural flexibility. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype chip achieves an average energy efficiency of 285.4 TOPS/W at 0.55 V in the convolution mode, delivering a $2.67\times $ improvement over the state of the art and demonstrating its efficiency and scalability for low-power, highly integrated satellite navigation and positioning applications.

item.title: A 90.9-dB SNDR Fourth-Order Fully Passive Bandpass Current-Integrating Noise-Shaping SAR Light-to-Digital Converter
item.description: This brief presents a fully passive fourth-order bandpass (BP) light-to-digital converter (LDC) using a current-integrating (CI) noise-shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) architecture for optical sensor interfaces and BP digitization. The proposed BP LDC achieves a sharp in-band noise suppression of −28 dB with a single-channel CI NS-SAR quantizer with passive gain and direct “ $z\to -z^{2}$ ” transformation. Inheriting the advantages of the CI-SAR architecture, it offers inherent antialiasing, dynamic range (DR) extension, and minimizes the analog front-end (AFE) duty cycle, achieving high power efficiency for direct light-to-digital conversion. A prototype, fabricated in a 180-nm process, achieves a 90.9-dB signal-to-noise-distortion ratio (SNDR) and a 107.2-dB DR in a 500-Hz bandwidth. The power consumption is 35.41- $\mu $ W, resulting in a FoMSNDR of 162.4 dB and a FoMDR of 178.7 dB without a separate transimpedance amplifier.

item.title: CLPA: A Clustering-Based Low-Power Accelerator for Energy-Efficient Matrix Multiplication
item.description: Efficient matrix multiplication is pivotal to minimizing the energy consumption associated with large language model (LLM) inference. In this work, we propose the bit-constrained Hamming clustering (BCHC) algorithm, an innovative approach designed to enhance energy efficiency in matrix multiplication. By imposing constraints on Hamming distance and position, the BCHC algorithm increases bit-level sparsity to $1.71\times \sim$ $ 1.78\times $ . Based on the BCHC algorithm, we design a sign decoder (SDecoder) to reduce the additional external memory access (EMA) and clustering-based processing element (CBPE) to leverage the bit-level sparsity after clustering. At last, we propose a low-power accelerator, named clustering-based low-power attention calculation accelerator (CLPA). Tested on multiple LLM benchmarks, CLPA achieves $2.05\times $ to $2.19\times $ GOPS/W improvement compared to Stripes and $1.20\times $ to $1.27\times $ GOPS/W improvement compared to Cambricon-C in energy efficiency.

item.title: A 23.5–46.5 GHz Gm-Boosting Feedback LNA With 2.7-dB NF and 14-mW Pdc in 28-nm CMOS
item.description: This paper proposes a high-performance two-stage broadband low-noise amplifier (LNA) for millimeter-wave applications. A new transformer is introduced between the gate of the common-source transistor and common-gate transistor of the input stage, which not only improves the input impedance at high frequency, but also mitigates the instability risk brought by $g_{\mathrm {m}}$ -boosting technique. A modified transformer is used in inter-stage matching network to boost the transconductance of the following transistor for gain enhancement. A shunt RC negative feedback cascode topology (SRCF-CT) is introduced in the output stage to optimize gain flatness. With these three main improvements, flat gain performance and low noise figure are achieved in a broadband frequency range. Implemented in TSMC 28-nm bulk CMOS process with a core area of 0.118 mm2, the LNA consumes only 14 mW DC power. Measured results show that a peak gain of 22.4 dB is achieved within a 3-dB bandwidth from 23.5 to 46.5 GHz. The input return loss ( $S_{11}$ ) is better than -10 dB over the 3-dB bandwidth. The measured NF is 2.2-3.6 dB with an average of 2.7 dB. The input 1dB gain compression point (IP1dB) ranges from −21.8 to −18.6 dBm in the entire gain bandwidth, resulting in a high OP1dB of −2.6 to 0 dBm.

item.title: A Compact Slew-Rate-Enhanced Class-AB Buffer Amplifier Using Internal Current Reuse for Display Column Drivers
item.description: High-resolution and high-frame-rate display systems impose increasingly stringent timing constraints on column-driver buffer amplifiers due to the drastic reduction of 1-horizontal (1-H) time. Although slew-rate enhancement (SRE) is essential to meet these constraints, conventional SRE techniques rely on explicit slew-sensing circuits and dynamic current sources (DCSs), introducing unavoidable static current and area overheads that severely limit scalability in multi-channel column-driver ICs. This paper proposes a compact SRE class-AB buffer amplifier that improves large-signal transition speed through transient-only internal current reuse, without external sensing circuits or DCSs. Slewing detection and enhancement are embedded directly into the signal path using only two diode-connected transistors, which remain inactive during steady-state operation, achieving zero static-current penalty and negligible area overhead while preserving the traditional amplifier’s stability. Fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process, the proposed amplifier achieves a $2.1\times $ slew rate improvement (from 0.8 V/ $\mu $ s to 1.7 V/ $\mu $ s) under a 3.3-V supply and a 30 pF load, while maintaining an identical static current of $2.2~\mu $ A. The additional area required is only $2~\mu $ m2 (0.3% increase), with no change in overall layout dimensions. Measurements demonstrate that the proposed amplifier meets the 1-H timing constraint of a 4K display operating at 120 Hz. To evaluate scalability in highly replicated analog systems, this work analyzes the trade-off between slew-rate performance and implementation overhead. The results demonstrate that the proposed design achieves sufficient slew-rate improvement to meet the target timing requirement with zero additional static current and minimal area overhead, ensuring highly scalable operation for next-generation, high-resolution display column-driver ICs.

item.title: Area-Efficient Low-Power Self-Biased Three-Stage OTA Fabricated in 0.6-μm IGZO-on-Plastic Technology
item.description: This work presents a high-efficiency three-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) fabricated in a commercial 0.6- $\mu $ m Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide (IGZO) thin-film transistor (TFT) technology on a flexible plastic substrate. The architecture leverages a fully self-biased differential input stage combined with a reverse nested Miller compensation with nulling resistor scheme to ensure robust stability under up to 40-pF loads. Operating from a 3-V supply, the OTA consumes only $60~\mu $ W while driving a 40-pF load, achieving a measured DC gain of 41.2 dB, a unity-gain bandwidth of 200 kHz, and a phase margin of 60.7°. Time-domain measurements demonstrate a 1%-settling time of $21~\mu $ s and a slew rate of 94 V/ms, with an output swing exceeding 83%. The self-biasing scheme and compensation strategy provide high resilience against process, voltage, and multi-die variations. This design occupies an active area of only 0.042 mm2, and achieves a power consumption of $60~\mu $ W with a small-signal Figure of Merit of 133.3 kHz $\cdot $ pF/ $\mu $ W, establishing a new performance benchmark for plastic electronics.

item.title: A 65-nm Compute-in-PUF Engine for On-Chip Learnable Anomaly Detection Using 2T--2T PUF Arrays
item.description: With the rising threats of side channel attacks and complexities of both on-chip and ambient environment, it is demanding to incorporate on-chip learnability into side channel attacks anomaly detection. This will enable offline-trained models to adapt to the new power profiles of emerging side channel attacks schemes, workloads, and varying environments. Existing side channel attacks detection techniques often fall short in in-situ learning or pose excessive on-chip integration challenges due to resource and data demands. This paper presents a novel neuromorphic “compute-in-Physical-Unclonable-Function” architecture, validated in 65 nm CMOS, designed for side channel attacks detection with on-chip learning capability and optimized area, energy and data overheads. We harness the physical unclonable function based key generator as a hyperdimensional encoder, enabling few-shot learning capabilities. The test chip achieves a detection accuracy of 97.2% and demonstrates true adaptability, restoring accuracy by up to 52% within a 5 ms after workload change. By unifying the security primitive and the compute engine, our design is achieve $7.5\times $ transistors reduction compared with an equivalent SRAM-based system while only imposing a 23.4% area overhead for the entire on-chip learning module. This work demonstrates a practical, silicon-proven solution that offers scalable, efficient and, adaptive security.

item.title: Stable Filtering ADCs
item.description: We present a general model that unifies the analysis of continuous-time and discrete-time filtering analog-to-digital converters. The model is based on a control perspective, where a high-gain analog filter is stabilized by a digital control system. From a general state-space representation, we derive explicit constraints on the filter parameters that guarantee bounded-input, bounded-output stability for each filter state. We propose a design methodology where the high-level filter design is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, enabling systematic co-optimization of filter topology, transfer function, and control scheme. For a given filter order and oversampling ratio, we compare different filter topologies and control schemes with respect to signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity to component variations. Compared to multi-bit sigma-delta modulators, our numerically optimized designs achieve comparable signal-to-noise ratio using only single-bit quantizers, with guaranteed state-wise bounded-input, bounded-output stability.

item.title: A Multi-Coarse Single-Fine 0.9-V 100-MS/s 14-bit SAR ADC With 5-Vp-p Input Range Achieving 70.3-dB SNDR and 171.3-dB FoMs
item.description: This paper proposes a 100MS/s 14-bit Multi-Coarse Single-Fine (MCSF) SAR ADC with 5Vp-p input range and a 0.9V supply for all circuits excluding the sampling block. The MCSF architecture is designed to efficiently handle high-voltage input signal swings with a low-voltage ADC, eliminating the need for an input buffer, while minimizing energy consumption. The architecture, which employs four separate Coarse ADCs along with a Fine ADC to perform the quantization, improves the input range of the ADC by a factor of 3.2. This effectively relaxes the noise requirement, thereby improving the power efficiency of the ADC. As a result, this work consumes only 21.9% of the switching energy compared to a conventional design. Fabricated in a 28nm CMOS process, the proposed ADC achieves an 82.4dB SFDR and a 70.3dB SNDR at Nyquist with 4.01mW power consumption, leading to a state-of-the-art 171.3dB Schreier FoM.

item.title: Noise-Power-Linearity Trade-Offs in Bandpass Active Filters and Bandpass Continuous-Time Pipelined Analog-to-Digital Converters
item.description: A bandpass continuous-time pipeline (CTP) ADC is an alternative to an active bandpass filter followed by an ADC. This work compares power-noise-linearity trade-offs in a bandpass filter+ADC with those in a bandpass CTP. We show that the latter overcomes fundamental limits of noise and linearity present in an active bandpass filter. Our analysis is validated via macromodel and transistor-level simulations in a 65 nm CMOS process.

item.title: A 200-MS/s Multi-Event TDC With Gated-DLL-Based Coarse/Fine Conversion and Event-Driven Phase Encoding for d-ToF Applications
item.description: This article presents a multi-channel, multi-event time-to-digital converter (TDC) with a highly-scalable architecture designed for direct time-of-flight (d-ToF) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensors with large-scale single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays. The proposed TDC features an ultra-low-dead-time event arbitration mechanism combined with a gated delay-locked loop (DLL) with an event-driven phase encoding scheme, enabling simultaneous coarse and fine timing measurements with a high conversion rate, thereby minimizing dead time between captured events. The shared architecture among 17 TDC channels significantly reduces on-chip area and power consumption, while the proposed ultra-low-dead-time coarse $/$ fine conversion technique ensures high throughput for sensors operating under high photon flux conditions. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS technology, the TDC achieves coarse and fine timing resolutions of 10 ns and 156.25 ps at a low reference clock frequency of 100 MHz, covering a 2.56- $\mu $ s dynamic range. The measured coarse and fine conversion rates are 600 MS $/$ s and 200 MS $/$ s, leading to a scalability figure-of-merit (FoM) of $42.64~1/$ fJ $/$ mm2, which is the highest among TDCs designed for d-ToF applications. The worst-case differential nonlinearity (DNL) and integral nonlinearity (INL) are measured as $+ 0.13/-0.09$ LSB and $+ 0.66/-0.78$ LSB, respectively.

item.title: An Event-Driven Dual-Mode 1280×1024 Cryogenic Infrared Vision Sensor for Adaptive Energy-Efficient Motion Perception
item.description: This paper presents an event-driven, dual-mode cryogenic infrared vision sensor that features a two-step time-encoding (TE) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and a high-speed frame difference (FD) for motion detection. To enable always-on scene-adaptive motion perception with power optimization, the vision sensor is reconfigurable, supporting two operation modes: 1) Precise Imaging (PIM) and 2) Motion Detection (MD). In PIM mode, a two-step TE ADC is proposed for small-pixel-pitch infrared focal plane arrays (IRFPAs). The coarse conversion utilizes pulse frequency modulation (PFM) with an area-efficient true single-phase clock (TSPC) counter. This PFM employs a non-periodic-reset architecture to enable multi-subframe fusion and fine conversion of time-to-first spike (TFS), thereby improving the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) within a limited pixel area. In MD mode, a high-speed FD-based 1.5-bit event detection is implemented, using subframe coarse conversion without incurring additional memory cost or frame-rate loss. Compared with PIM mode, MD mode reduces power consumption by approximately 40% by deactivating fine conversion and partial output channels. A $1280\times 1024$ prototype with a 15- $\mu $ m pixel pitch was fabricated using a stacking process, in which the digital readout integrated circuit (DROIC) was implemented in a 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process and interconnected with the HgCdTe IRFPA via indium bumps. In PIM mode, the prototype achieves 83.2dB SNR with a power consumption of 115.4 mW at 30.5 frames per second (fps) (1.49 pJ $\cdot \mu $ m2/step). In MD mode, with an 8-bit coarse conversion for event detection, the sensor consumes 58.83 mW at 976.6 fps (3.5 fJ/pixel-event), achieving the best event FoM among reported event-driven infrared vision sensors.

item.title: A Differential Resonant Ultrasound Pulser in 180 nm BCD: Fundamental Limits and Design Considerations
item.description: This article presents the design of a differential resonant pulser implemented in 180 nm BCD process for PMUT-based ultrasound applications. By employing a precisely timed switching scheme together with differential resonant operation, a novel voltage step-up methodology is developed. A key contribution of this work is the first comprehensive, phase-by-phase analytical treatment of the pulser operation. This analysis reveals critical inter-phase coupling mechanisms that are not captured by conventional simulation-based approaches. It identifies two previously overlooked design limitations: 1) ac current leakage inherent to back-to-back DMOS configurations; and 2) an unavoidable timing offset caused by finite on-resistance ( ${R}_{\mathrm {on}}$ ) between the inductor current peak and the capacitor voltage zero-crossing during discharge. These effects establish fundamental performance boundaries for resonant pulsers. Measurement results validate the proposed design, achieving a 17.7 V output from a 5 V supply ( $3.5\times $ voltage step-up) and a 71.7% reduction in power consumption. The measured performance represents state-of-the-art and shows excellent agreement with both theory and simulation.

item.title: A 40k fps 99.5 dB Wide Dynamic Range PWM Image Sensor Featuring a Low-Power Pixel Array
item.description: This paper presents a $500\times 1000$ array pulse-width modulation (PWM) sensor with wide dynamic range, low power consumption fabricated in 110-nm CIS FSI process. The prototype demonstrates key performance metrics with $17\mu $ m pixel pitch, achieving 40k fps full-resolution imaging while maintaining 21.5% fill factor and $20.40\times 11.08$ mm2 die size. The chip achieves 99.5 dB dynamic range while maintaining 37.5 pJ/pixel $\cdot $ frame energy efficiency under dark conditions. Dynamic power management scheme implements adaptive row activation achieving 0.75W dark-current power consumption. By encoding scene information in compressed bit-stream format, the sensor provides high spatiotemporal resolution while eliminating redundancy in raw data transmission. Quantizing light intensity directly in the temporal domain, instead of the voltage domain, enables a wide dynamic range to be achieved at a substantially lower power cost. This parallelized architecture shows strong potential for intelligent vision systems requiring real-time high-speed processing capabilities.

item.title: A Multi-Bit CMOS Characterization Platform for One-Million Resistive Switching Devices
item.description: Emerging resistive switching devices require large-scale characterization, yet existing approaches often rely on external instrumentation, small custom arrays or architectures that lack autonomous current sensing. This work introduces MELITA, a fully integrated CMOS platform that supports parallel characterization of more than one million two-terminal devices. Fabricated in $\mathrm {180~ nm }$ CMOS, the chip combines on-chip DACs, current-to-voltage converters, column-parallel ADCs, and a digital controller into a unified readout architecture. Automated current ranging extends measurable input currents across five decades, while programmable read voltages enable flexible test conditions. Measured results confirm both block-level and system-level operation, with a 12 bit digital output. Application-specific experiments demonstrate the ability to extract I-V curves directly from large-scale two-terminal device arrays composed of passive top-metal structures, validating scalability and readout functionality of the platform. Although noise limits the effective Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) to 43 dB, the platform uniquely integrates array access, analog front-end, digitization, and control into a scalable test vehicle. MELITA therefore provides a practical step toward realistic benchmarking of resistive devices within system-level CMOS environments.

item.title: Design of a 3--7GHz Clockless Self-Mixing IR-UWB Receiver Front-End With a Sub-10-Ps TDC
item.description: This paper presents a non-coherent self-mixing front-end circuit designed for a clockless, low-power, wideband impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) receiver. The design features a transformer-based low-noise amplifier (LNA) that enhances the gain and the bandwidth through $\boldsymbol {g_{m}}$ -boost and magnetic coupling techniques, followed by a shunt-peaked radio-frequency amplifier (RFA) for further band extension, and a compact self-mixer for envelope detection. To support hybrid high-order demodulation, a two-stage time-to-digital converter (TDC) with sub-10-ps resolution extracts both the rising and falling edges of the received pulses after evelope detection and comparison. The proposed design was fabricated in 40-nm CMOS technology, achieving sensitivities of -64 dBm at 1.344 Gb/s and -55 dBm at 2.016 Gb/s, an energy efficiency of 6.7 pJ/bit, a power consumption of 13.62 mW, occupying an active core area of $0.376~\text {mm}^{2}$ .

item.title: A 0.2--12-GHz Fast-Settling Wideband Frequency Synthesizer With Stage-Switching Frequency Extender and Continuous Compensation PFDCP
item.description: A fast-settling wideband frequency synthesizer (FS) for multiband communication applications is presented. Through the integration of a wideband low-noise VCO with the proposed stage-switching frequency extender (SS-FEX), the FS achieves continuous frequency coverage from 0.2 GHz to 12 GHz with high area efficiency. Equipped with inter-stage switches and wake-up transistors, the SS-FEX supports a division ratio range of (2 or 3)N (where N = 1-4) with low power consumption, without degrading the phase noise performance of PLL. The optimized E-TSPC divider adopted in the SS-FEX enables robust divide-by-2/3 operation over a wide frequency range. To accelerate locking, a continuous compensation phase-frequency detector and charge pump (CC-PFDCP) is proposed, which fully utilizes the idle time after the PFD reset. Fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process, the proposed synthesizer occupies a compact wideband technique (W.T.) area of 0.12 mm2 and achieves an rms jitter of 139.6 fs. The measured locking time is $13~\mu $ s. Consuming 19.3 mW overall, the FS achieves a figure of merit (FOM ${}_{\mathrm {J}}$ ) of 244.2 dB, a FOMJ,T of 269.9 dB, and a W.T. area FOMJ,T (FOM ${}_{\mathrm {J,T,A}}$ ) of 279.1 dB.

item.title: A Long-Retention-Time 3T Embedded DRAM in 40-nm Bulk CMOS Process With Super-Boosted Write and Three-Reference-Voltage Read Schemes
item.description: Due to short data retention time (RT), eDRAM requires frequent refresh, posing a challenge for low-power applications, especially in sub-65nm process nodes. To address this issue, a Super-Boosted-Write (SBW) 3T eDRAM design is proposed. In this design, the parasitic capacitive coupling effect of the storage node is leveraged to increase the storage data voltage difference. To minimize area and reduce charge leakage caused by writing two adjacent rows in a short period, a source-line-shared eDRAM array with interleaved addressing is introduced. By analyzing the statistical distributions of data’s storage voltage and the transistor’s threshold voltage, based on the binary detection theory, a three-reference-voltage read scheme is further proposed to reduce the bit error rate (BER) by up to three orders of magnitude, enabling longer RT. Fabricated in 40nm, the silicon measurements demonstrate that, under the same 0.1% BER and $85~^{\circ } $ C, the proposed SBW 3T eDRAM achieves twice the retention time and half the power dissipation compared to state-of-the-art eDRAM designs.

item.title: A 236-nW LFSR-Based Asymmetric Clonable PUF Group With Peer-to-Peer Response Equivalence
item.description: Traditional physically unclonable function-based authentication models that use challenge-response pairs suffer from high storage overhead and lack support for multi-party authentication. We propose an asymmetric clonable PUF group for decentralized authentication, wherein both master and slave instances generate peer-equivalent responses. In this scheme, only the master instance provides intrinsic entropy derived from fabrication variability, which supplies both a seed for the shift-alignment-resistant dual-LFSR and a separate static entropy. The master instance synchronizes with the slave instance via unidirectional ports, after which the ports are permanently disabled. At runtime, the generated values serve as PUF-rooted authentication tokens and can be bound to a fresh verification transcript through locally derived session keys. The fabricated core demonstrates high statistical performance, resilience against machine-learning and algebraic attacks, and low measured idle power of 236 nW with 11.8 pJ/token response-generation energy. These results indicate the feasibility of secure, always-on multi-party authentication in resource-constrained edge devices.

item.title: An Energy-Efficient Time-Step Configurable SNN Processor for Object Detection With High Spatiotemporal Reuse Heterogeneous SAU/MAU Cores
item.description: The energy efficiency of object detection processors based on traditional artificial neural networks (ANNs) is constrained by intensive multiply-accumulate operations and frequent memory accesses. Spiking neural networks (SNNs), characterized by biological plausibility, multiplier-free computation, and inherent sparsity, offer a promising alternative for energy-efficient inference. However, deploying SNNs for high-resolution object detection faces three key challenges: 1) long time-steps to maintain accuracy; 2) redundant weight access across time-steps; and 3) substantial external memory access (EMA) incurred by intermediate feature maps (FM). To address the above challenges, a dedicated SNN processor is presented with three contributions: 1) a customized short time-step quantized spiking YOLO (QS-YOLO) model, achieving 65.80-72.90% mAP on VOC2007 within only 1–4 time-steps through a progressive temporal compression (PTC) and quantization framework; 2) a novel weight-locally-distributed stationary spatio-temporal sequential interleaving (WLS-STS) dataflow, enabling single weight access across all time-steps while supporting flexible time-step configuration without loss of processing element (PE) utilization; and 3) a workload-aware dynamic global buffer allocation strategy to eliminate FM-EMA. The proposed processor incorporates a heterogeneous dual-core architecture, comprising a spike-driven accumulate unit (SAU) and a multiply–accumulate unit (MAU), to efficiently accelerate both spiking and non-spiking operators in QS-YOLO. Implemented on XCVU13P FPGA, the processor achieves a peak energy efficiency of 146.48 GOPS/W at 100MHz. Compared with existing object detection FPGA processors, the proposed processor achieves state-of-the-art energy efficiency.

item.title: BVDT: A 28-nm LUT-Assisted Transformer Accelerator With Basis-Vector Compression and Decomposed Computing
item.description: Transformer-based neural networks are pivotal to emerging vision and natural language processing tasks. Despite their success, accelerating these models remains challenging due to their immense computational and memory requirements. Traditional methods, such as sparse attention computing, alleviate some of these burdens but fall short in addressing the complexity of diverse operators and the significant storage overhead caused by large model parameters and low data reuse rates. In this work, we propose BVDT, an energy-efficient Transformer accelerator that exploits inherent matrix redundancy to overcome these limitations through four key innovations. First, BVDT introduces a novel basis-vector decomposition technique that compresses model size by over $25\times $ , supported by unified memory management. Then, it incorporates a dual array core architecture, powered by LUT-assisted computing, featuring an optimized lookup code fetch and LUT programming mechanism. In addition, BVDT employs a block-wise post-fusion mapping method that seamlessly links the compression pattern and computing architecture. Finally, BVDT utilizes a private-to-private highway data-path for multi-core systems, enabling a LUT stationary dataflow that significantly reduces the memory access overhead. Consequently, BVDT provides a task-agnostic optimization across diverse Transformer operators under various workloads. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS technology, the accelerator achieves an exceptional area efficiency of $4.35~TOPS/mm^{2}$ , a $5.1\times $ improvement over prior state-of-the-art solutions. Moreover, BVDT also achieves $1.4\times $ to $3.6\times $ regarding energy efficiency, offering a promising solution for Transformer-based applications.

item.title: A Full-Digital Heterogeneous Computing-in-Memory With Dual-Bit Serialized Weight Stream and Ping-Pong Computing for Efficient Transformer Acceleration
item.description: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across various computer vision tasks. However, the self-attention mechanism in transformers incurs high processing loads and costly off-chip data movement in conventional von Neumann architectures. This paper proposes a full-digital heterogeneous Computing-in-Memory (CIM) in-situ hybridizing differential RRAM and SRAM to enable efficient on-chip weight storage and flexible row-column dual-directional access for efficient transformer acceleration. A Ping-Pong computing dataflow is introduced to maximize the throughput density by allocating static and dynamic computations across CIM macros. A low-toggle weight tuning algorithm is proposed to minimize the dynamic power under the dual-bit-serial CIM scheme by introducing only small weight rounding distance. Besides, a patch-channel skip mechanism is used to reduce the redundant computing for dynamic matrix with high sparsity. Experimental results on different transformer models show that the proposed DBS-CIM architecture reduces layer-wise computing energy by up to 59.9% compared to conventional digital CIM. Compared to prior homogeneous CIM designs, it achieves $2.0\times $ to $3.3\times $ higher end-to-end energy efficiency, and outperforms existing heterogeneous CIM designs by $2.13\times $ in computational density.

item.title: A High-Performance Neural Rendering Accelerator With Dual-Lane Micro-MLPs and Hierarchical Latency-Hiding Scheduling
item.description: While Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have transformed 3D vision, their prohibitive computational and memory demands restrict real-time deployment on power-constrained edge devices. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel neural rendering accelerator that orchestrates three architectural innovations to maximize throughput and energy efficiency. First, to resolve computation bottlenecks, we introduce a Dual-Lane Backend Mechanism utilizing Fused Micro-Multi-Layer Perceptrons (Micro-MLPs), boosting sample processing throughput by $1.98\times $ . To minimize memory traffic through data locality, we implement Multi-Resolution Spatial Partitioning Strategy with Adaptive Ray Clustering, effectively exploiting scene sparsity, and improving the cache hit rate up to 95%. Finally, to hide memory latency, a Hierarchical Scheduling Framework with Proactive Prefetching is employed, reducing execution stalls by 77%. Experimental results on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) prototype demonstrate 94.7 frames per second (FPS) at $800\times 800$ resolution within a 6.4 W power consumption, achieving a 42.2% frame rate improvement over state-of-the-art FPGA implementations. Furthermore, application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) synthesis results based on 28 nm CMOS technology projects a peak throughput of 440 FPS with a power consumption of 268 mW, translating to a highly competitive energy efficiency of 0.76 nJ/pixel. By delivering superior energy efficiency while maintaining high visual fidelity with a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) > 30 dB, this work paves the way for ubiquitous, photo-realistic rendering on the edge.

item.title: A Frequency-Domain Vision Accelerator for High-Resolution Object Detection on RAW Data
item.description: While high-resolution inputs improve recognition performance, they impose significant hardware overhead due to the computational intensity and memory bandwidth demands of conventional image signal processing (ISP). This inefficiency primarily stems from the structural mismatch between pixel-level ISP operations and the semantic information required by back-end neural networks. To address this, we propose an end-to-end RAW-based frequency-domain vision pipeline designed for efficient high-resolution detection. Under normal imaging conditions, the proposed pipeline bypasses the full human-perception-oriented ISP and directly processes RAW sensor data through lightweight channel mapping and a hardware-friendly approximate discrete cosine transform (DCT). To minimize front-end data movement, we reformulate the color-space transformation within the frequency domain and retain only a compact set of task-relevant low-frequency coefficients. Furthermore, we employ a multiplier-less, shift-and-add-based arithmetic architecture to simplify control logic and enhance energy efficiency. The pipeline is fully compatible with standard convolutional neural networks, requiring no architectural changes to the back-end detector. We validated the design using a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based prototype on the Xilinx ZCU102 platform integrated with a YOLOv3-Tiny detector. The system achieves real-time processing of $6144\times 4096$ RAW inputs at 33.18 frames per second (FPS). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed frequency-domain approach maintains detection accuracy comparable to RGB-based pipelines while significantly reducing hardware resource utilization and power consumption.

item.title: A 1.8-Gb/s PSK-UWB CMOS Transceiver With Extended PPM/PWM Modulation and Costas-Loop Carrier Synchronization
item.description: This article presents an energy-efficient phase-shift keying ultra-wideband (PSK-UWB) transceiver for high-throughput brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). By combining multi-bit pulse position modulation (PPM) and pulse width modulation (PWM), a 6th-order extended PPM/PWM modulation (E-PPWM) is proposed to achieve a high data rate of 1.8 Gb/s with a relaxed symbol rate. In the transmitter, a time-domain E-PPWM pulse directly modulates the phase of carrier for up-conversion, resulting in PSK modulation embedded with E-PPWM which achieves an improved signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared with amplitude-based hybrid modulation. The carrier power is simultaneously spread with a wideband triangular modulation profile to comply with the UWB spectrum mask. The receiver employs a Costas loop to perform real-time carrier recovery as well as PSK demodulation, achieving low-latency data transmission. A prototype PSK-UWB transceiver implemented in 65 nm CMOS achieves a data rate of 1.8 Gb/s with a power consumption of 28.2 mW and an energy efficiency of 15.7 pJ/b.

item.title: Transient Synchronization Stability Analysis of Renewable Energy Grid-Tied System Under Three-Phase Short-Circuit Faults by Unified Theory
item.description: Three-phase short-circuit faults pose the most severe threat to the power system transient stability. In this paper, a unified theory is developed for the transient synchronization stability (TSS) analysis of renewable energy grid-tied system (REGS) considering complete low-voltage ride through (LVRT) process, under typical three-phase short-circuit faults in single-line and double-line systems. Within the framework of the unified theory, a systematic analysis for diversified fault scenarios is performed, including a unified model based on the 3-stage generalized swing equation (GSE) and a TSS assessment method based on the 3-step improved equal-area criterion (IEAC). The nonlinear models considering the complete LVRT process are established for each stage and further unified into the same form of GSE by focusing on the phase-locked loop dynamics. Relying on the unified model and the IEAC, the calculation results of critical clearing angle and critical clearing time are found to show the errors within $1~\%$ . Further the effect of key parameters in the TSS is evaluated, and the feasible region under these key parameters is obtained. Numerical simulations and experimental results perfectly validate the unified theory and demonstrate its effectiveness in the TSS analysis of REGS under the three-phase short-circuit faults, where complete LVRT transient process cannot be ignored.

item.title: DRAM-Compatible Deterministic B2S Conversion Using Time-Weighted Comparison and DRAM-Resident Templates
item.description: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes numerical values as long binary bitstreams and performs arithmetic through simple bitwise logic, making it naturally suited to processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures. A key bottleneck is the conversion from compact binary numbers to these long bitstreams, known as binary-to-stochastic (B2S) conversion. When this conversion is performed outside the memory array, the resulting bitstreams must be written back into DRAM, introducing data-movement overheads that dominate end-to-end energy and latency. This work presents a deterministic in-DRAM B2S framework that performs this conversion inside DRAM banks without modifying the 1T1C cell array or sense amplifiers (SAs). The design repurposes standard SAs to perform magnitude comparisons through a time-weighted wordline-activation mechanism, and employs deterministic threshold templates stored as static DRAM rows. A three-phase pipeline coordinates initialization, RowClone-based broadcast, and weighted comparison to generate column-parallel bitstream outputs across an activated row, scalable across banks. Evaluations show that the resulting bitstreams provide statistical properties and task-level accuracy comparable to Sobol sequences, a widely used high-quality reference in SC, across the tested bitstream lengths and workloads. System-level analysis indicates that generating bitstreams directly inside DRAM avoids the bandwidth cost of moving them across the memory channel, reducing end-to-end energy and latency by more than $2\times $ relative to external CMOS-based generators in the evaluated configurations, and providing a latency advantage over binary in-DRAM PIM at low-to-moderate precisions. These results demonstrate a practical path toward DRAM-compatible SC.

item.title: HE-FR: A High-Efficiency Fault-Resilient Framework for Stuck-at-Faults Mitigation in ReRAM-Based In-Memory Computing
item.description: ReRAM-based in-memory computing (IMC) architectures enable efficient neural-network inference on edge devices, due to their high density and non-volatility. However, ReRAM is prone to the stuck-at faults (SAFs) which would distort weight mappings and reduce model accuracy substantially. To tackle this problem, a high-efficiency fault-resilient (HE-FR) framework is introduced in the paper, which couples layered-precision quantization based on the generalized gaussian distribution cumulative distribution function (GGD-CDF), preserving weight distributions with the minimal information loss. Further, a fault-aware weight re-decomposition method is proposed. Specifically, a Q-agent-based method is proposed for sparse SAFs, which employs offline reinforcement learning to construct a globally optimized hash table with reduced compilation complexity, while incorporating both weight matching and cell-state stability into the reward function to suppress electro-stress. For dense SAFs, we exploit a greedy search over the remaining cells to provide rapid and accurate mappings. Experimental results show that GGD-CDF quantization improves accuracy by 2.18% over Float32. Under fabrication faults, HE-FR surpasses a fault-free method by 12.97% and accelerates compilation by $197\times $ with only 0.024% picojoule-level energy overhead. In electro-stress evaluations, HE-FR reduces performance degradation by 46.27%. It demonstrates that the proposed framework has advantages in robustness, efficiency, and reliability.

item.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Electro-Thermal Co-Optimization Framework for PDN in 3-D Integrated Microsystem With Embedded Microchannel Heatsink
item.description: This paper presents a machine-learning-assisted software framework for circuit and system-level electro-thermal co-design of three-dimensional integrated circuits. The framework targets power delivery networks (PDNs) with embedded TSV microchannel structures and unifies equivalent circuit modeling, surrogate-based performance prediction, and intelligent optimization into a design automation workflow. To enable fast power integrity evaluation, a physics-based matrix equivalent circuit formulation is developed to extract the frequency dependent RLGC parameters of densely coupled TSV arrays under coolant perturbation. The proposed model achieves approximately 90% runtime reduction over full-wave electromagnetic simulation while keeping the impedance error within 6.6%. For large scale PDN synthesis, a Transformer-Pointer reinforcement learning solver trained with proximal policy optimization is introduced for decoupling capacitor placement in high-dimensional combinatorial spaces, reducing the PDN impedance by 20%. For thermal design space exploration, a tri-model hybrid semi-supervised surrogate is integrated with NSGA-II to accelerate the multi-objective thermal integrity optimization process by predicting thermal performance indices. The proposed framework provides a scalable software methodology for integrated modeling, analysis, and optimization of advanced 3D power delivery and thermal management systems.

item.title: Channel-Aware Behavioral Power Modeling of CMOS OOK Transceivers for Wireless Network-on-Chip Systems
item.description: Wireless Network-on-Chip (WNoC) systems enable low-latency communication in many-core platforms through short-range wireless links. However, the power consumption of integrated transceivers (TRXs), dominated by that of the RF front-end circuitry, remains a major challenge. Moreover, the optimal operating frequency is still unclear, as bandwidth, energy efficiency, and technology maturity must be balanced. This work presents a channel-aware behavioral modeling framework to estimate power consumption and identify energy-efficient operating points in non-coherent On-Off Keying (OOK) TRXs over a wide frequency range. The approach leverages survey data from CMOS implementations to derive frequency-dependent power models for key TRX sub-blocks, including the power amplifier (PA), oscillator, mixer, low noise amplifier (LNA), and envelope detector (ED). By incorporating the frequency-dependent channel loss into the TRX power budget, the model captures system-level power trade-offs across operating regimes. The analysis reveals a frequency-dependent shift in power dominance between the transmitter and receiver: oscillator- and ED-dominated regimes at lower frequencies transition to PA- and LNA-dominated behavior at higher frequencies. Furthermore, the energy-per-bit landscape exhibits sweet spots and a model-based global minimum, indicating that optimal operation cannot be achieved by optimizing transmitter or receiver independently. Overall, the proposed framework enables rapid and physically grounded exploration of power scaling with frequency and channel conditions, providing practical guidelines for energy-efficient design of high-frequency wireless links for WNoC systems and beyond.

item.title: Hardware-Efficient Architectures and Low-Complexity Algorithms for Multi-Coset Sub-Nyquist Sampling-Based Wideband Spectrum Sensor for Dynamic Spectrum Access
item.description: This paper proposes an implementation-friendly algorithm for multi-coset sub-Nyquist sampling-based wideband spectrum sensing (WSS). To the best of authors’ knowledge, this algorithm has been designed for the first time using the iterative power method with deflation technique and the exponential fitting test to reduce its computational complexity. In addition, it has been incorporated with a memory-efficient and hardware-friendly interpolation algorithm. In response to the suggested WSS algorithm, a hardware-efficient architecture for wideband spectrum sensor (WBSS) is presented in this work from system to micro-architectural level. Furthermore, a dual-clock architectural technique has been suggested for signal acquisition in the proposed WBSS architecture to enhance the sensing bandwidth. In this paper, computational complexity and performance analyses of the suggested WSS algorithms are presented in a comprehensive way. Finally, the WBSS architecture is implemented on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC-ZCU104 FPGA-board that is used in a real-world test setup for functional validation of the measured results. Compared to state-of-the-art implementations, the proposed WBSS has achieved 33.75% better hardware efficiency, $3.6{\times }$ lower memory requirement, and $6.34{\times }$ wider sensing bandwidth.

item.title: Bi-Directional DFE-Based Maximum Likelihood Sequence Cross-Detection in a 112-Gbps PAM4 Wireline Transceiver
item.description: As wireline data rates continue to scale, pre-cursor inter-symbol interferences (ISIs) become increasingly significant due to channel dispersion and bandwidth limitations. Conventional decision feedback equalizers (DFEs) are inherently limited to cancel post-cursor ISIs only, while feedforward equalizers (FFEs) suffer from fundamental trade-offs, either reducing signal swing at the transmitter or amplifying noise at the receiver. To address these problems, a bi-directional DFE (BiDi-DFE) architecture is introduced to equalize both pre-cursor and post-cursor ISIs without noise amplification. Leveraging the opposite decision-propagation directions of the two DFE paths, a maximum likelihood sequence cross-detection (MLSCD) scheme is further proposed to detect error events and selectively enable maximum likelihood sequence detection (MLSD), improving energy efficiency. A 112-Gbps DSP-based wireline transceiver deployed over a 45 dB insertion-loss channel achieves a bit error rate (BER) reduction from $1.5\times 10^{-6}$ to $1.6\times 10^{-7}$ using BiDi-DFE, and further to $7.5\times 10^{-9}$ with MLSCD, incurring only an estimated 20-mW power increase in post-layout compared with a 1-tap DFE while achieving an estimated 40-mW power saving in post-layout relative to a full-state MLSD (FS-MLSD). These results indicate that the proposed BiDi-DFE and MLSCD framework offers a scalable solution for future high-loss, high-speed wireline transceivers.

item.title: Lyapunov-Based Adaptive Control With Semi-Saturation Mechanism for Bilinear Buck-Boost Converters
item.description: This paper addresses robust voltage regulation of an inverting buck–boost converter subject to parametric uncertainty and unknown load-induced disturbances. Passivity-based, sliding-mode, and predictive schemes from the literature commonly rely on state observers or precise knowledge of the load resistance, and their performance tends to degrade as the duty ratio $u(t)\in (0,1)$ approaches the bilinear singularity at $u = 1$ . To overcome these limitations, we propose a continuous, observer-free adaptive controller built on three key elements: a Lyapunov-based regulation law that updates a single scalar parameter directly from the measured variables $(i_{L}, v_{o})$ , with no model inversion or online identification; a smooth semi-saturation mechanism that enforces $u(t) \lt 1$ at all times, preserving control authority near the singularity; and rigorous closed-loop guarantees of practical stability under bounded disturbances and asymptotic convergence when disturbances vanish.
